title: Two men charged with murder of Bexhill cyclist
text:
Two men have appeared at Lewes Crown Court, charged with the murder of a Bexhill cyclist, Sussex Police have said.

Stephen McMurdo, 71, was struck by a ball bearing as he cycled along Bexhill Road, St Leonards, on the evening of 10 July 2020, police said. He suffered a serious head injury that resulted in left-side paralysis.

Mr McMurdo died in October 2025. Joshua O'Toole, 29, of Maidstone, and Lloyd Powell, 32, of no fixed address, were originally charged with grievous bodily harm in connection with the incident on 28 July 2023, police said.

Both men pleaded not guilty to the offence of murder and were released on court bail, with a further hearing date to be confirmed, police added.

Stephen's wife, Jaki, paid tribute to him. She said: "Steve was a wonderful husband, father and brother who loved, supported and understood me. He made me laugh a lot. We were married for 25 years and although the last five were different, he never lost his sense of humour. We will always miss and love him."

title: Councillor calls 500-home Bexhill plan a 'disaster zone waiting to happen'
text:
A Bexhill town councillor has described proposals for a potential 500 new homes in the town as a 'disaster zone waiting to happen'.

Cllr Paul Wilson, who represents Collington ward, raised his concerns at a town council meeting discussing Rother District Council's Local Plan, which sets out where new homes, businesses and shops can be built between now and 2042.

He said he was astonished that the draft plan still included 'the nearly 500 houses on and around the back of Chestnut Meadow in Ninfield Road', and questioned how the roads could cope: 'It is absolutely astonishing that they're relying upon Peartree Lane and St Mary's Lane to back up Ninfield Road. It is a congestion and a disaster zone waiting to happen.'

Cllr Wilson said building up to 500 homes would swell the area's population to around 3,900 residents, and that the site is near the Sidley stream, which links down to Egerton Park and the Polegrove, where flood prevention work is under way.

Cllr Paul Plim, who represents Central ward, said somebody planning the development 'has got to bite the bullet and say, right, if you want these houses you've got to build the road structure to support it'.

title: Donations top £10,000 for Isfield farm shop after raid
text:
Donations totalling more than £10,000 have flowed in to help a family farm in Isfield after thieves ransacked its shop, the owners said.

Balaclava-wearing men broke into South Brockwells Farm Shop on Friday night and took all the chilled and frozen produce, including packages made up for Christmas, along with kitchen and butchery equipment including knives, prompting owners Arron and Chrissy Wells to close the business.

Ms Wells said the pair had asked friends to help them raise about £1,500 to make good some of their losses, and were 'shocked and delighted' to find the total quickly rose above £10,000 and could top £11,000.

The family now plans to open the farm shop in December and to hold a party 'for all the amazing people who have helped us'.

Ms Wells said the dogs woke them to the intrusion: 'It was absolutely terrifying. Neither of us can sleep now, wondering if this is going to happen again.' Police were called but could not track down the car that left the scene. On the same night, a garage at Allens Farm, Five Ashes, was also broken into, with power tools and meat taken from freezers.

title: Hastings council budgets £1,937,861 for St Mary in the Castle in 2026/27
text:
Hastings Borough Council has budgeted spending of £1,937,861 on the Grade II* listed seafront building St Mary in the Castle in the 2026/27 financial year, with the majority set to come forward as capital spending.

Cllr Julia Hilton, the council's deputy leader and lead member for regeneration, set out the figures in response to a written question from Claire Carr, a former borough councillor and chairwoman of the St Mary in the Castle Community Trust.

The total is made up of £1,247,000 on repairs to the road/roof of Pelham Crescent and £617,000 on 'pre-marketing works'. To date the council has spent £12,332 and £18,755 in those areas, and a forecast shows the budget is still expected to be spent by the end of the year.

The council had also planned to spend £49,150 on day-to-day revenue costs associated with the building, which includes security. To date it has spent £62,452 and is expecting to spend £81,447 by the end of the financial year. It had also planned for a £24,711 repairs and renewals budget; to date it has spent £32,351 but does not currently expect further expenditure in that area before the end of the year.

Ms Carr raised a supplementary question at the meeting on 9 November. She said it had been four years since the doors closed at St Mary in the Castle and a year since it was put on the heritage at risk register, and asked when a report on the condition survey was due to come to cabinet. Cllr Hilton said she had not received a detailed update from officers and added it was 'time we had an update on the next stages', with some of the work having to be done by the council to enable the building to be 'fit for anybody to take on board'.

title: On this day 1918: The Armistice reaches the East Sussex papers, 1918
text:
When news of the Armistice reached Britain on 11 November 1918, newspapers in East Sussex reported on the joy and the solemn reflection of the county.

With the end of hostilities agreed early in the morning of 11 November and planned to take effect at 11am in France, the fighting was about to draw to a close. It was not a surprise when word of the end spread, it had become clear that the German Army had been defeated in the field and that an allied victory was imminent. Even so, the Armistice signalled the end of the fighting but was not a guarantee that the war was over; it would not be until the Paris Peace Conference in 1919 that the war was brought to an end for Britain.

None of the county's papers, the Eastbourne Chronicle, the Eastbourne Gazette or the Hastings and St Leonards Observer, was published on the day of the Armistice announcement, so editions appeared in shops several days later. The Observer was fairly restrained: the Armistice was not mentioned until page 6 of its 16 November edition, in an article outlining how the town had greeted the news.

The coverage showed the people of East Sussex to be hugely relieved and jubilant at the end of the war and the fighting, after four years of conflict. There were also clear fears over what the coming months would hold, whether the peace could be maintained, and concern for the men still in France and for families whose loved ones would not return home.

title: Residents to have say on East Sussex supported housing strategy
text:
People in supported housing across the district can have their say on how it should improve, Rother District Council has said.

The Supported Housing Strategy for East Sussex is being developed by Eastbourne, Hastings, Lewes, Rother, Wealden and East Sussex Councils. It will set out how the councils work with partners to improve supported housing and make sure it meets the needs of local people, the council said.

The proposed priorities include planning for the supported housing people will need, working with housing providers to continue improving quality, making sure housing is safe, suitable and well managed, and making sure residents receive the right support and have a say in the services they use.

The councils want to hear from supported housing residents, their families and carers, housing providers and staff working in health and care. The survey closes on 21 December 2026, on the East Sussex County Council website.

title: Bexhill Leisure Centre named UK Active Awards finalist
text:
Bexhill Leisure Centre has been named a finalist for Regional Centre of the Year at the UK Active Awards, one of the leisure industry's leading national award programmes.

The centre, operated by Freedom Leisure on behalf of Rother District Council, said the recognition comes as the council makes a significant investment in the facility's infrastructure to support its long-term future and help it continue providing leisure, health and wellbeing services for local residents.

Toby Reed, Freedom Leisure's area manager in Rother, said: "We're incredibly proud of the team at Bexhill Leisure Centre."

title: Little Common Library marks annual volunteer lunch
text:
Volunteers and supporters came together in Bexhill for Little Common Library's annual fish and chip lunch, its chairman Connor Winter said.

The gathering, held at Little Common Community Centre, was a chance to celebrate the work of the people who give their time to keep the library running, he said. "We are incredibly fortunate to have such a dedicated group of people who give their time to support our library and the wider community," Mr Winter said.

Steve Johnson, from Bexhill Heritage, delivered a presentation on the Brassey family and their connections to the town. The library is open on Tuesdays from 9.30am to 3.30pm, and on Fridays from 9.30am to 12.30pm.

title: Rye Bonfire named among the UK's best Bonfire Night displays
text:
The Rye and District Bonfire has been named among the best Bonfire Night displays in the country, The Argus reports.

The Telegraph featured the event in a list of top displays across the UK, describing it as one that rivals the better-known Lewes Bonfire Night and praising its drums, fire torches and fireworks finale. The tradition is entirely self-funded by volunteers through collections, sales and a crowdfunding page.

This year's bonfire takes place on Saturday 14 November. The torchlit procession starts at 7pm through the cobbled streets, passing under the Landgate Arch, and ends at Rye Salts, where the bonfire is lit at 8pm and fireworks follow at 8.15pm.

Organisers say it is a family-oriented evening, and ask that no fireworks are discharged before, during or after the procession, and that discarded torches are not picked up.

title: Hastings brothers set for Nepal peaks for veterans' charity
text:
Two brothers from Hastings are heading to the Himalayas to raise money for a local veterans' charity.

Josh and Jake Bruton, both former British Army soldiers, told BBC Radio Sussex they are setting off on Friday to climb Lobuche East and Island Peak in Nepal, both of which are more than 6,000 metres high. They are raising funds for the East Sussex Veterans Hub, a Hastings-based charity that supports former military personnel, including those who are homeless and those with mental health issues and addictions.

"We want to raise as much money as we can climbing heights. For us, it's important to us to help veterans in our home town," they said, as reported by the BBC.

It is not their first challenge: in 2025 Joshua cycled across America from Miami to San Diego, and the brothers completed the Hastings Half Marathon in March carrying a 40kg log on their shoulders.

title: Westfield player Michael Rwabigwi called up for Rwanda
text:
A player at a tenth-tier English football club has been called up to represent his country.

Westfield FC, of the Southern Combination League Division 1, said Michael Rwabigwi has been named in Rwanda's under-23 squad for the Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers against Cameroon.

The club said: "It's an incredible achievement for Mikey and a hugely proud moment for everyone connected with Westfield FC." A spokesman added the club was contacted by the federation asking if it could release him, calling it "a deserved call-up".

Rwanda play Cameroon at home on Wednesday 11 November, with the return fixture six days later.

title: Plans for 42 new homes by St Leonards' Bannatyne's Spa Hotel
text:
Outline permission has been submitted to build up to 42 homes on land at Bannatyne's Spa Hotel in Hastings Road, St Leonards, according to the latest Hastings Borough Council planning applications.

The application (reference HS/OA/26/00608) seeks residential development, including associated roads and amenity spaces, with all matters reserved for future consideration apart from the means of access.

The submission is one of several in the latest round-up, which also lists a single-storey rear extension at 16A Branksome Road, St Leonards, and plans to install four condensers at 6 Bank Buildings, Station Road, Hastings.

title: Battle Bonfire 2026: 'Guy Feaux' effigy takes a swipe at AI
text:
Battle High Street became a 'river of fire' on Saturday night as people turned out for the town's annual bonfire celebrations, the Hastings Observer reported.

Following a torch-lit procession down the High Street, crowds gathered around a large bonfire on the Abbey Green to watch a fireworks display. Bonfire societies from across the county took part, including Hastings, Rye, Lewes, Robertsbridge and Staplecross.

This year's effigy was a robotic Guy named 'Guy Feaux', a swipe at artificial intelligence. Battle Bonfire is organised by the Battel Bonfire Boyes and traces its traditions back 380 years, with the earliest recorded celebration dating to 1646.

title: Nineteen-year-old opens her own beauty salon in Bexhill
text:
Grace Guenigault, 19, has opened her own beauty salon in Bexhill, the Hastings Observer reported.

The Glam Studio is in Village Mews, Little Common, and opened on 31 October. Grace said she has had a passion for the beauty industry and wanted to create 'a welcoming space where clients could feel relaxed, comfortable and confident'.

She offers eyelash extensions, lash lifts and tints. 'I'm 19 and feel really excited and proud about starting my own business,' she said, and added that it is important for locals to support independent businesses because 'they help bring character, diversity and a sense of community to the area'.

title: On this day 1883: Electric street lights trial switched on in Hastings
text:
This week in November 1883, a trial of electric street lights in the town was switched on.

The lights were switched on on 12 November 1883, after the council gave the go-ahead for a trial in August 1882, according to a Hastings history feature in the Sussex Express.

Before that, a council meeting in January 1881 had thrown out a proposal to examine the cost of using electricity to power the street lighting rather than gas. Electric lights had first come into large-scale use nationally in 1879 and by 1881 were in use in most cities. Many of the councillors were shareholders or directors of the highly profitable Hastings Gas Company, so they threw out the electricity suggestion, the feature reports. The council's agreement with the gas company was to run until 1883.

Then in January 1882 a group of prominent local businessmen and councillors met to discuss setting up a local electric light company. Many of these people were also shareholders in the gas company, and they agreed to hedge their bets by setting up the Hastings and St Leonards Electric Light Company a few months later. They were to use the 'Brush' system of lighting, and they acquired a site for a power station in Earl Street, the building of which is now a carpet and furniture warehouse.

In January 1884 electric lights were installed on Hastings Pier.

title: Two Sussex police officers charged over assault of detained man
text:
Two Sussex Police officers have been charged with assault occasioning actual bodily harm over an incident involving a man detained in hospital under the Mental Health Act, according to the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC).

PC Richard Harris, 36, and PC Lorenzo Fenu, 28, are to appear in court on 10 November, jointly charged with the offence. The IOPC said the charge relates to an incident on 16 April 2026, when the officers allegedly used unlawful force on a man who had been detained in hospital under the Mental Health Act, and injured him.

The watchdog said it began its investigation following a mandatory referral from the force. At the end of its investigation in September, it referred a file of evidence to the Crown Prosecution Service, which authorised the charges.

title: Swansea Sound to open tour at The Piper in St Leonards
text:
Swansea Sound, who feature members of Heavenly and Talulah Gosh, are to kick off their tour in St Leonards at The Piper on 13 November.

The show comes on the back of the band's new album Pre-Post-Truth, their third record. A spokesman described it as 'a collection of twelve new punk and power-pop tunes with a lot more lyrical bite than you get from the average indie band'.

The line-up includes Hue Williams (ex-The Pooh Sticks), Amelia Fletcher and Rob Pursey (Heavenly), Bob Collins (The Dentists) and Ian Button (Death In Vegas, Railcard). The band has recorded sessions for 6Music, Radio X and WFMU in New York, and has just completed a tour of the US.

title: Police launch manhunt for man wanted for recall to prison
text:
Police have launched a manhunt for a man wanted for recall to prison and are asking anyone who sees him to call 999.

Sussex Police issued an urgent public appeal on Sunday evening, naming the man as Gurvinder Singh, 39. The appeal says he is "wanted for recall to prison for breaching the terms of his licence" and is currently serving a sentence for robbery, and that he has links to Brighton and Crawley.

Anyone who sees him is being asked not to approach him and to call 999 immediately, quoting crime reference 47260234461, the force said.

The appeal was posted on Sussex Police's Facebook page and is aimed at people across Sussex, including Hastings and the Rother valley.

title: St Leonards' Becky Palmer wins Christmas tree flinging at Catsfield
text:
A 27-year-old from St Leonards has won the women's title at the Christmas tree flinging contest at Catsfield Christmas Tree Farm near Battle.

Becky Palmer, 27, reclaimed the women's crown with a throw of 7.88m, ahead of Louise Thompson, 36, also of St Leonards, who threw 5.65m. The men's title went to James Gardiner, 37, of Hailsham, with a throw of 10.45m, which bettered his own winning distance of 9.1m from last year.

Farm owner Clive Collins said the contest, which began in 2020, has become "a much-loved part of our Christmas build-up". Adults had to hurl a six-foot Norway spruce, while smaller trees were used in the under-10 and under-16 categories.

Both champions won £150 and a tree-shaped wooden trophy.

title: Fire-hit St Leonards convent site goes to auction at £1.7m
text:
A former convent in St Leonards that was damaged in a major fire earlier this summer is going on the market, with a guide price of £1.7 million and a potential major housing scheme for the land.

The Convent of the Holy Child of Jesus in Magdalen Road is being offered by auctioneer Allsop, with the vacant freehold site under the hammer on 16 December.

The sale follows a fire on 9 July which police treated as arson, at which eight fire engines were called and two teenage boys were later arrested, the Argus reports. The site covers about 11.7 acres and includes the former convent and chapel, a Gothic building, a gateway lodge and a gateway, with structures listed at Grade II and Grade II*. The Grade II* chapel was not affected by the fire.

According to the sale documents, the land is allocated for a heritage, landscape and residential-led regeneration with an indicative capacity of 200 homes. Any development would have to secure repair and restoration of the listed buildings and protect the nuns' cemetery. Hastings and Rye MP Helena Dollimore said the community was 'deeply distressed' by the fire.

title: The Plough in Rye named among Britain's best pubs
text:
A pub in Rye has been named among the best in the country, with recognition for what the guide calls an unpretentious country pub.

The Plough was named in the top 100 of The Good Food Guide's 2026 list of the country's best pubs. The guide ranked it at number 38, the highest in Sussex, and described it as 'an unpretentious country pub noted for its seasonal, locally sourced food'.

It won high marks for uniqueness, deliciousness and strength of recommendation, and was rated 'very good' for warmth.

Set on a rural stretch of road three miles from Rye, the pub is praised for its 'glorious' location, a garden where, in fine weather, 'sheep baa-ing while you eat' beckons, and 'scuffed floorboards, plain tables and wood-burners' inside. Paintings by Sussex artist William Warden are said to 'bring a lovely local connection to the venue'.

title: Hastings runner to take on 55-mile ultramarathon in jeans
text:
A 21-year-old from Hastings is about to take on one of the country's toughest challenges, and he is doing it in denim.

Peter Nagle, 21, will run 55 miles across the South Downs in a pair of jeans next month to raise money for men's mental health. On 5 December he will tackle UK Ultra's Winter on the Downs, a single-loop race with more than 7,000ft of climbing. That is over two marathons back to back, the Hastings Observer reports, in actual jeans rather than just a layer of denim over running kit.

The jeans come from The Perfect Jean, a New York-based stretch denim brand that has backed the challenge and will follow his training.

All the money raised goes to Andy's Man Club, a men's mental health charity that runs free, judgement-free talking groups for men across the UK every Monday at 7pm. Peter, who previously ran the Hastings Half Marathon in jeans for the same cause, said: 'If this gets one person talking to a mate who's struggling, that matters just as much as any donation.'

title: St Leonards and Hastings properties sell at Clive Emson auction
text:
A mixed-use property at 32 Kings Road, St Leonards, has been sold before the auction in one of the latest Clive Emson Auctioneers sales, which listed 174 lots across southern England.

The freehold had been offered with a guide price of £310,000 to £320,000 at the auction, which ended on Thursday 5 November, but was sold in advance. It comprises two ground floor commercial units and two separately accessed residential flats above, all let under a full repair and insuring lease for a 16-year term at £33,282.64 per annum, ending in February next year.

Auction appraiser Jade Flood said the property was in a prominent position on Kings Road, "within easy reach of local shops, amenities and the seafront", and that her buyer agreed by completing the purchase ahead of the sale.

At the same auction, a four-storey mixed-use property at 187 Queens Road, Hastings, went under the hammer at £178,000 freehold, exceeding its guide price. It comprises ground floor retail accommodation with a mezzanine storage room, a maisonette over three upper floors, plus basement accommodation and a rear yard.

Director and senior auction appraiser Sam Kinloch said there had been "considerable pre-sale interest" in the property, which "translated into competitive bidding".

title: Local band raises £3,000 for Warming Up the Homeless
text:
A group of local musicians have raised around £3,000 for Warming Up the Homeless in the last couple of years by giving their CDs away free and encouraging audiences to donate to the charity instead.

The Other Band, which has been playing for over a decade, performs an eclectic mix of Americana from many different decades. It consists of Julian Graff on mandolin, guitar and vocals, and Lee Hill on guitar, harmonica and vocals, with frequent guest musicians Dave Fricker on bass and Stu Alexander on accordion.

Warming Up the Homeless is a registered frontline charity supporting homeless people on the South Coast from Hastings to Eastbourne. Operating since 2015, it supports over 1,400 men, women and children a week, providing daily outreach support, food banks and welfare advocacy.

The arrangement means the band gets its music heard while the charity benefits from the donations, according to a feature in the Hastings Independent Press. The Albatross Club in Bexhill and Barnaby's Lounge in Hastings have been particularly supportive, promoting both the band and the charity.

title: Hastings swimmer plots route to 2028 Channel crossing
text:
Hastings swimmer Sarah Milne has completed an endurance training camp in Dover with The King's Swimmers and, in her latest diary for the Hastings Independent Press, says she is now preparing for a solo Channel crossing attempt in 2028.

During the week-long camp she swum 35 kilometres back and forth from Swimmer's Beach near the ferry port. Kevin Murphy, one of The King's Swimmers' directors and coaches, told her that he and the team believed she could swim the Channel solo in 2028, and offered to write her weekly training plans.

Ms Milne had not swum proper front crawl in years before May, when she discovered Fish 2 Water open-water training in Eastbourne. She has since joined Hastings Seagulls Masters, and is now in her second week of longer pool sessions three times a week, alongside back-to-back weekend endurance swims.

title: Camber Sands holiday park ranked among worst in UK
text:
Camber Sands Holiday Park, near Rye, has been named one of the lowest-rated holiday parks in the country.

The park was ranked ninth lowest out of 242 parks in an analysis of Google reviews by family holiday company Ski Famille, according to The Argus.

title: Have your say on renewal of five gated paths in Hastings and St Leonards
text:
Hastings Borough Council is asking for views on plans to renew gating orders for five public rights of way in Hastings and St Leonards.

The gates were introduced in March 2024 to help reduce antisocial behaviour and improve safety in these areas, and government guidance requires gating orders to be reviewed every three years to ensure they continue to deter it.

The five locations are Valentine's Passage, linking Shepherd Street with North Street in St Leonards; Laser Lane, linking Kings Road to Cross Street in St Leonards; Prospect Passage, from Havelock Road to Priory Square in Hastings; Trinity Passage, linking Robertson Street with Claremont; and Hoads Wood Road to Pilot Road.

A council spokesperson said the proposed renewal was "based on considerable evidence".

title: Hole Park near Rye promises a top Christmas tree crop after summer drought
text:
One of the Rye area's longest established Christmas tree growers is promising a top-quality harvest for the second year in a row.

While some growers in southern England have reported significant losses from this year's prolonged dry spell and late frosts, the Hole Park Estate in Rolvenden, near Rye, is preparing for another strong season, with very few trees lost and exceptional quality in those being harvested from this week.

The plantations, established in the mid-1960s, are said to have been helped by the High Weald's heavy clay soils, which retained moisture through the drought.

Estate owner Edward Barham, the second generation in the family to manage the Christmas tree plantations, said the location in the Weald had worked in their favour, and that this year's crop was among the very best he could remember. The estate covers around 100 acres, with up to 20,000 young trees planted each year and around 16,000 harvested annually.

The estate's Norway Spruce was named runner-up in its category at the British Christmas Tree Growers Association's 2026 National Awards.

title: Seagull artist's gull-version masterpieces on show in Crown pub
text:
Hastings artist Bill Greenhead, known for his cartoon-style paintings of chip-stealing seagulls, has an exhibition in the Snug bar of the Crown in Hastings Old Town.

Bill creates seagull-themed versions of masterpieces such as the Mona Lisa, and his paintings include versions of Admiral Nelson and of David Bowie as Aladdin Sane, transformed into gulls. His 'Gull Culture' series has proved hugely popular, with the paintings invariably including stolen chips.

He moved to Hastings in the early 2020s and began oil painting after receiving an online course voucher as a birthday gift during lockdown. He has exhibited during the Coastal Currents festival and his work featured in an installation at Hastings railway station.

The exhibition can be viewed until 26 November.

title: Plans for up to 125 homes at Robertsbridge mill site
text:
Proposals to build up to 125 homes on the Hodson's Mill site in Robertsbridge are set to go before Rother District Council's planning committee on Thursday, 12 November. The plans come from Homes England, the government's housing and regeneration agency.

Part of the development would come from converting the former mill building and redeveloping the Grade II listed oast house on the site. The mill building would be turned into eight two-bed flats, a one-bed flat and two retail or community units, while the oast house would be dismantled and rebuilt as two three-bedroom homes.

The largely brownfield site, vacant since 2001, has long been allocated for development. Homes England took it over in March 2024 after earlier plans were deemed undeliverable.

The current proposal extends into green field land at the north of the site, and council planning officers are recommending approval. A financial viability appraisal says the development could not support affordable housing, and officers say it has been independently scrutinised.

title: Call for interest in future use of Sandhurst Recreation Ground
text:
Hastings Borough Council is asking sports clubs, groups and organisations to register their interest in the future of Sandhurst Recreation Ground. The council wants to know how much demand there is for the sports pitches, which organisations would like to use the site, and whether it could be managed or developed by the community.

The site, traditionally used for football and cricket, is expected to be considered for all sports, and the council is working on a longer-term strategy covering the next three to ten years.

Cllr Glenn Haffenden, the council leader and lead councillor for sport and leisure, said the council wants to bring the pitches back into regular use to provide better sports and leisure opportunities for Hastings residents.

Groups wanting to visit the site can arrange a visit by contacting the council, and full details are on the council's website.

title: Ada the Asda car park fox has been relocated to a safer home
text:
Ada, the friendly fox that made her home in an Asda car park in Hastings, has been moved to a safer place by a wildlife charity. The fox had become well known for approaching shoppers, begging for food and trying to climb up people's legs.

While popular with many locals, her complete lack of fear of humans worried those who cared about her welfare. A vehicle was deliberately driven at her on one occasion, and as the weather turned she grew bolder.

Wildlife Matters caught her and took her to the Mallydams RSPCA centre at Hastings, where she was checked over. She showed no signs of illness, but when she was released in another area she made her way back to the car park.

With the help of the Fox Angels Foundation, a new home was found. After an earlier capture attempt failed, she was finally contained in a moment of distraction while being fed by a couple, and taken to her new home.

title: Bexhill mayor celebrates new school councillors at Glenleigh Park Primary
text:
Glenleigh Park Primary Academy in Bexhill hosted a special assembly to celebrate student leadership, with the Mayor of Bexhill, Cllr Memish Huseyin, in attendance. The visit marked the appointment of the school's newly elected school and eco councillors, following an election campaign that involved all pupils.

The mayor spoke with the new school councillors about leadership and his own journey to becoming mayor, while the children asked questions about the role. He praised the pupils' enthusiasm for democracy and citizenship.

Headteacher Libby Barnard said the school council elections give pupils the chance to develop leadership skills and understand democratic processes.

The school also marked its results for the 2025/26 year, with 80% of Key Stage 2 pupils reaching the combined reading, writing and maths expected standard, which puts it in the top 10% nationally.

title: MP joins launch of Hastings & St Leonards Poppy Appeal
text:
Helena Dollimore, the MP for Hastings, Rye and the villages, has joined veterans and volunteers at the launch of this year's Hastings & St Leonards Poppy Appeal, held in Tesco, raising money for veterans and their families.

The launch carried a poignant note. Local veteran Bryan Hunter was due to receive an award in recognition of 35 years of dedicated fundraising, having staffed the Tesco stall every year during the poppy appeal period without a single day off. He died just days before the launch.

Last year the Hastings & St Leonards Poppy Appeal raised £66,808 for the Royal British Legion.

Ms Dollimore said: "It was an honour to join the launch of the Hastings and St Leonards Poppy Appeal today and pay tribute to all the local veterans and volunteers who make it happen each year." She added that the launch was a moment to remember Bryan, whom she described as a stalwart of the community who dedicated himself to the appeal every year and who would be so missed.

title: Cabinet to consider £1.5m playground funding on Monday
text:
More than £1.5m to improve playgrounds across the town is set to be considered at the council's Cabinet meeting on Monday evening.

The funding comes from the government's Pride in Place Impact Fund, the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government's Playground Fund, and the council's own budget, which was committed as part of its 2026-27 budget process.

Council leader Cllr Glenn Haffenden said residents had made clear that improving play provision was "really important". Cllr Jo Walker, lead councillor for Climate, Nature and Green Spaces, added that the council is working with housing associations to improve play areas on their land and in their developments.

Following Cabinet approval, work will begin to appoint a contractor and to confirm which playgrounds, alongside Alexandra Park as a destination playground, will benefit from investment.

title: Hastings Draft Local Plan: Convent site open for comment until 12 November
text:
The deadline for the public to comment on the Hastings Borough Council's Draft Local Plan is Thursday 12 November, and one of the most argued-over parts of it is what happens to the Convent of the Holy Child Jesus in Lower Bohemia.

The convent caught fire in July 2026. For months beforehand, residents made complaints to the council about the site's vulnerability, the Hastings Online Times reports. The Draft Local Plan now proposes demolishing the East Wing, the red and white building near White Rock Gardens, to make way for more and higher-density housing.

Under the process known as Regulation 19, the public have six weeks to comment on the plan, which will be finalised in June 2028 and will guide planning in the borough until 2041. The Save the Convent group has put forward its own proposals for the site.

title: From Hastings to the Royal Albert Hall: Count Us IN set to perform
text:
Fifty-one young musicians from Hastings and St Leonards will take the stage at the Royal Albert Hall on 10 November as part of the Music for Youth Proms.

They will join more than 1,000 young performers from across the UK and are the only group from East Sussex selected to perform. All are members of Count Us IN Community Music, a programme run by ExploreTheArch and supported by Youth Music that provides free instruments, equipment and tuition.

Count Us IN began within the Four Courts Connect community programme on Stonehouse Drive and now reaches 11 schools and colleges across the area. Music for Youth waived the group's participation fees in recognition of the barriers many participants face, and the trip has been helped by the Chalk Cliff Trust.

title: Hastings care home rated 'Good' across all five CQC areas
text:
Mountside Care Home in Hastings has been rated 'Good' in all five areas assessed by the Care Quality Commission.

The home on Laton Road, part of ACI Care, achieved 'Good' for being safe, effective, caring, responsive and well-led, as well as its overall 'Good' rating.

The home manager, Lisa, said: "I am incredibly proud of our team. Achieving Good in all five areas is a wonderful recognition of the care, effort and dedication colleagues bring to Mountside every day."

title: Bexhill family featured in Chestnut Tree House hospice film
text:
The family of a six-year-old Bexhill boy who died of a brain condition has featured in a new film as part of a campaign to show the vital role of hospices.

Kai was supported by Chestnut Tree House for several years until he died just before Christmas 2025. His mums, Leanne and Sara, describe how the hospice helped them make memories over his life, from hydrotherapy to a summer festival and dry-slope skiing.

Kai's story is part of the Show Your Love appeal by Southern Hospice Group, which also runs Martlets in Hove and St Barnabas House in Worthing. The charity said just 14 per cent of its costs are covered by NHS grants, with funding relying heavily on local communities.

title: West Hill Lift closed for urgent surveys and repairs
text:
The West Hill Lift has been closed for essential surveys and repairs, according to the Hastings Independent Press.

The funicular railway, which opened in 1891 and retains its original wooden Victorian coaches, runs through a tunnel, which makes maintenance particularly difficult.

It is one of the town's 'crown jewels' and a popular tourist attraction, with scenic views stretching round to Beachy Head in the west and out across the English Channel.

A Hastings Borough Council spokesperson apologised for the inconvenience and said the council could not provide a timeline for when it will reopen, due to the nature of the works.

title: BFI film course sees 18 young people make their first film in St Leonards
text:
A group of 18 young people under 19 have taken part in a six-day film course in St Leonards, making an original short film from scratch as part of the BFI Film Academy South East Introductory Course.

The programme, part of a national push to attract fresh talent to the industry, is delivered locally by The Bright Foundation, an arts education charity set up by Academy Award-winning costume designer John Bright, and taught by industry professionals including writing mentor Trix Worrall, creator of the Channel 4 show Desmond's, who live in Hastings.

The course covered scriptwriting, direction, acting, production, post-production and costume and prop design, with no previous film experience required. The film, called Going Out West, is a dystopian thriller in which AI has taken over the world, with the script mainly written by a Rye College student, and team members included a student at East Sussex College's Hastings campus working as assistant director.

Bright Foundation CEO Polly Risbridger said the course hands over creative control to the young people, who 'literally take on every role, learning all the skills along the way'.

title: GP link worker helping Hastings residents with long-term conditions get active
text:
Active Hastings' specialised 'Link Worker' is helping residents with long-term health conditions become more active, bridging the gap between healthcare and community-based activity, according to the Hastings Independent Press.

The role was created in 2022. It was originally funded by the Hastings and St Leonards Primary Care Network through to 2026 and is delivered in partnership with Hastings Borough Council and East Sussex County Council.

A simplified referral system lets GPs and other health professionals refer people to Active Hastings, opening up a wide range of activity opportunities across Hastings rather than a single activity, with the link worker matching each person to what suits their needs.

Jas, the GP link worker, has introduced new sessions where provision was lacking, including chair-based yoga, seated strength and gym and circuit sessions for people with neurological conditions, and helped set up 'safe' exercise spaces for women. One 56-year-old woman living with chronic back pain, who had felt disconnected from activities she once enjoyed, is now back into regular yoga.

title: Man pleads guilty to shoplifting across Hastings and Rother
text:
A 45-year-old man from Winchelsea Beach has been charged in connection with a series of shop theft offences across Hastings and Rother.

His arrest and charges follow an investigation by local officers. Hastings Police said the charges relate to the theft of approximately £100 worth of clothing from Marks & Spencer in Hastings, the theft of approximately £330 worth of food and alcohol from Jempson's in Rye, and the theft of approximately £261 worth of food from Jempson's in Peasmarsh.

He appeared before Hastings Magistrates' Court on 27 October 2026, where he pleaded guilty to three counts of shoplifting. He was granted unconditional bail to allow for the preparation of pre-sentencing reports.

A Hastings Police spokesperson said: 'Shop theft has a significant impact on local businesses, staff and the wider community.' The force said it will continue to work closely with retailers across Hastings and Rother.

title: Driver jailed for 13 months after 104mph police pursuit ended in ditch
text:
A disqualified driver has been jailed for 13 months after leading police on a 31-minute pursuit through Hastings, Winchelsea and Rye that ended in a ditch in Iden.

Alexander Williams, 31, of Bembrook Road, Hastings, was sentenced at Lewes Crown Court on 28 October. He had been indicated to stop in The Ridge, Hastings, and crashed off the road through an apple orchard as the chase ended. A police stinger device had deflated his tyres before the black Range Rover came to rest.

Police said he was travelling at up to 104mph in a 60mph zone in wet conditions. He was also given 4 years and 5 months of a driving ban. Police said he had been disqualified only 18 days before the incident on 28 September.

Williams told police he had fled because he was on probation. He had also been caught driving while disqualified before, the court heard.

title: Labour ends cooperation with Greens on 11 councils
text:
Labour has withdrawn from power-sharing agreements with Green councillors in 11 local authorities, including Arun, Lewes and Wealden district councils in Sussex, over the party's ‘Zionism is Racism’ policy.

The Labour Party's national executive committee has ordered its councillors to end cooperation with the Greens in those 11 councils. The move follows an October ultimatum aimed at 18 councils; cooperation is to continue in Rother District Council, among others, according to the Hastings Online Times.

Labour chair Bridget Phillipson said: “Labour has been clear from the start that the ‘Zionism is Racism’ policy crosses a line and we cannot work with any party that supports it – at any level of government.” Groups with cooperation arrangements were asked to seek a “clear and unambiguous public statement” from the Greens rejecting the policy.

The Green Party said it was “hugely disappointed in moves designed by national parties to force local council leaders into jeopardising successful progressive partnerships that are delivering benefits for residents.”

title: Sculptor Leigh Dyer's steel fins go on sale at At Sea
text:
The metal sculptor behind several well-known works around Hastings has opened a new line for sale at the At Sea gallery in the Old Town.

Leigh Dyer made the commemorative winkle on Winkle Island, the Bale House Canopy at Hastings Country Park, the shiny snakes on the outsized chess pieces in George Street and the boat sculpture sunk into Pelham Beach, according to the Hastings Independent Press.

At Sea, an art gallery gift shop that opened in July at 52 George Street, is showing Dyer's work, which is not generally made for public sale, alongside a group of mainly Sussex-based painters and sculptors. Twelve steel fins, made of crib steel and about a foot high, are on sale there.

“I want the work I make in Hastings to help people see the beauty of the place, perhaps with fresh eyes,” Dyer said. “The fins were enjoyable to make and have sold quickly, I'll no doubt be making a new edition soon.”

title: Hastings council to consider Age Friendly strategy for older residents
text:
Hastings Borough Council has drawn up an Age Friendly Hastings Strategy and Action Plan, with proposals to make the town more accessible and inclusive for people aged 50 and over.

The plan will be considered by the council's cabinet on 9 November. If approved, it will guide work through to March 2028. The programme would receive £50,000 a year from Public Health, amounting to £150,000 over three years, with most of the money going to staffing.

The proposals include recruiting volunteers to check how accessible shops, pavements and public spaces are, improving community transport links, adding exercise classes aimed at preventing falls, and helping older people remain in their own homes.

The Argus reports that the proportion of Hastings residents aged 65 and over is projected to rise from 22 percent in 2026 to 28 percent by 2047, and that healthy life expectancy in Hastings is around five years below the East Sussex average.

title: Car wash owner sentenced over illegal workers
text:
A car wash owner in Hastings has been sentenced after illegal workers were repeatedly found at his business, Sussex Police said.

In October 2025, Sussex Police's Discovery team and partner agencies attended the business, operated by Ermir Halilaj, and identified a worker who, due to their immigration status, had no legal right to work in the UK. A second worker was identified at the business on a subsequent visit. Both workers were handed to immigration services.

Halilaj, 38, of no fixed address, pleaded guilty at Hastings Magistrates' Court on 19 August to two counts of employing a person with cause to believe they were disqualified from employment by reason of their immigration status.

On 22 October he was sentenced to six months' imprisonment, suspended for 12 months, and ordered to engage with the Probation Service and complete 100 hours of unpaid work. PC Jon Tree, from the Discovery Team, said: "Employers have a responsibility to carry out appropriate checks to ensure those working for them have the legal right to do so."

title: Ark Alexandra CCF wins three honours at Lord-Lieutenant's Awards
text:
Ark Alexandra Academy's Combined Cadet Force had a triple win at the Lord-Lieutenant's Awards Ceremony, held at Lancing College and attended by senior military personnel and civic representatives from across the region.

Captain Nick Burchell was honoured with a Lord-Lieutenant's Award in recognition of his outstanding contribution to the cadet movement over many years. He has recently taken on the role of Chair of the Sussex Combined Cadet Force Leadership Group.

Senior cadet Pippa Styring was appointed the Lord-Lieutenant's Cadet for East Sussex CCF, receiving a certificate and a badge she is entitled to wear on her uniform throughout her appointment.

Rounding off the evening, the unit was awarded the Irlam Trophy for its outstanding support for Combat Stress, the veterans' mental health charity. The trophy is named in honour of Lieutenant Colonel Tom Irlam MBE. The ceremony was reported to the Hastings Online Times by Carol Sales, from Ark Alexandra Academy.

title: Devolution measures to bring £8m to Sussex and Brighton
text:
Last week's budget included measures to give devolved local government in England a bigger share of its own tax revenues, the Hastings Online Times reports.

From the next financial year, local councils and mayoral strategic authorities in England will be allocated a larger share of business rates, and from 2028/29 areas with mayors will keep part of local income tax revenues. The government intends local and regional government to retain 100 percent of local business rates income by the end of the decade, with the transfer initially managed in a fiscally neutral way.

The Good Growth Fund will start operations in 2027/28 with an initial pot of £285m. The larger share, £165m, is earmarked for areas with a mayor in 2027, while £120m will be incubator funding for areas transitioning towards a devolution deal.

Sussex and Brighton, which are still in the transitioning phase, will get £8m from the Good Growth Fund. The county's acquisition of mayoral status is still 18 months away, and local government reorganisation has been pushed back by a further year.

title: Hastings' last wooden fishing boat 'Felicity' to be restored and displayed in Rock-a-Nore
text:
The last surviving wooden fishing boat from Hastings is to be restored and put on permanent display after a fund-raising campaign reached its target of £5,000. The 'Felicity', RX58, will be displayed on the piece of land opposite the Dolphin pub in Rock-a-Nore Road.

The clinker-built boat was constructed in 1980 by H J Phillips Boatbuilders in Rye and was originally named Our Pam and Peter, her construction once the subject of a BBC documentary. She was worked for many years by the brothers who own her, and was deregistered two years ago when she ceased work.

Peter Carney, who founded the Hastings Wooden Boats group and started the appeal, said the Old Hastings Preservation Society, the Fishermen's Museum and volunteers had worked together to save the boat. "Sincere thanks to everyone who contributed to reaching our target of £5,000 to save her," he said. A plan to turn her into an ornamental building for a private garden, which would have involved cutting her in half, had left her future in doubt.

title: Self-storage operator opens 44th site on Sedlescombe Road, St Leonards
text:
Self-storage specialist Cuboid Self Storage has opened its second site in Sussex, on Sedlescombe Road in St Leonards-on-Sea. The facility opened on 1 November and is the company's 44th site nationwide, joining its existing facility in Shoreham.

Tim Knowles, founder and managing director of FI Property Group, said Cuboid is the largest self-storage container business in the UK by capacity, and that demand for high-quality, secure and flexible storage facilities has continued to grow.

The site offers 20ft containers providing more than 1,100 cubic feet of secure space, gated access seven days a week from 6am to midnight, 24-hour CCTV monitoring and heavy-duty lock and key security.

title: Council to seek group to take lease of Hollington Community Centre
text:
East Sussex County Council is looking for a local group to take on the lease of Hollington Community Centre in Old Church Road, after saying the building needs significant investment to bring it back into good repair.

The centre opened in 1974 and is a registered charity. It is home to a table tennis club that has run there for 70 years, along with judo, short mat bowls, a social section and walking cricket. It has been listed as an asset of community value by Hastings Borough Council.

In a published report, the county council said the property is recognised as a community asset but requires significant capital investment, and that it cannot carry out the works itself or operates no council service from the building. It will run a bidding process to find a community or voluntary organisation able to take the lease and fund the repairs, the report said.

Local people attended a special meeting at the centre on 31 October to discuss its future. Cllr Will Chapman, a Hollington councillor, said the centre has served local people for decades and the town "cannot afford to lose such a valuable local asset."

title: Work begins on 27 'luxury flats' development in St Leonards
text:
Work has started on a scheme of 27 flats in St Leonards. Scaffolding is going up and the first foundations are being built on a West Hill Road site, according to the Hastings Observer.

The plot was first put forward for development by MPG (St Leonards) Limited in 2014 and the proposal was approved by Hastings Borough Council in October 2025. The site, of about 0.7 acres, went on the market for £795,000 earlier this year.

A statement published when the land was marketed described it as a consented site offering "a rare chance to deliver a landmark residential scheme of 27 exclusive luxury flats", with no on-site affordable housing obligations.

title: 'Write by the River' poetry exhibition opens at Rye station
text:
A new poetry and artwork exhibition called 'Write by the River' has opened at Rye railway station. It features poems and illustrations about the area's waterways, including the River Rother and River Tillingham.

Posters printed by Southern Railway are displayed in the station's ticket office waiting area, according to the Hastings Observer. The project was facilitated by StrongBack productions and supported by the Marshlink community rail partnership, which runs along the line between Hastings and Ashford International.

Writer Morgan Greenhalf said the idea was to bring together people who had never written before as well as those with experience, and introduce them to the river.

title: Storms strip Pett Level beach, exposing 1940s sea wall
text:
Storms Austen and Boelo have stripped away large sections of Pett Level's shingle beach defences, exposing for the first time in decades an old 1940s stepped concrete sea wall and a tarmac service road that had been buried beneath the shingle, according to the Hastings Independent Press.

The storms brought heavy rain and gusts of 60 to 70mph, and high tides stripped shingle along the stretch from Pett Level to Winchelsea Beach and Cliff End. Erosion has left a sheer five-foot drop near the grassy path on top of the sea wall where the beach used to be.

The speed of the beach's loss has triggered formal requests for emergency government intervention, not just to replace the shingle but to fund permanent defences. The beach and its surrounding land form part of the Dungeness, Romney Marsh and Rye Bay protected area.

title: One East Sussex reorganisation to proceed, with four Lewes wards moving to Brighton
text:
The Government has announced it is minded to proceed with local government reorganisation in East Sussex, Hastings Borough Council has said.

It proposes to implement the One East Sussex plan submitted jointly by Hastings and four other East Sussex councils, but with a significant change: four wards would be transferred from Lewes district into an expanded Brighton & Hove authority.

Under the revised timetable, elections to the new shadow authorities are expected in May 2028, with the new councils becoming operational in April 2029. The Government said both the original One East Sussex proposal and the modified option met all six of its criteria.

Councillor Glenn Haffenden, leader of Hastings Borough Council, said the One East Sussex plan would bring together the services of Hastings Borough Council and East Sussex County Council within a single new authority, but warned the transfer of four Lewes wards would be “a significant change for residents, staff and local services”.

title: Charity raises £4,000 to save Bexhill Hospital stroke rehabilitation service
text:
Becky, Sarah and Owen from the #DoItForJosh charity met the team at Bexhill Hospital’s Irvine Unit on Monday to mark the continuation of a vital local stroke rehabilitation programme.

The charity had reached its fundraising target of £4,000, stepping in to rescue a service that was facing closure due to a lack of funding. The money will enable East Sussex Healthcare NHS Trust and Active Sussex to continue delivering structured activity sessions for stroke survivors within the Irvine Unit.

The target was reached through community events earlier this year, including the Three Castles Ultra Marathon in May and the 4th annual Josh Alexander Cup in September, alongside public donations.

Josh’s mother and the charity’s chair, Becky, said the cause held a special place for them, as the charity’s co-founder and Josh’s father died following a stroke last year.

title: Cooden Beach Golf Club seeks permission for homes on part of its course
text:
Cooden Beach Golf Club is seeking planning permission to build housing on part of its course on Cooden Sea Road, according to an application to Rother District Council.

The proposal would be for four detached five-bedroom houses fronting Cooden Sea Road and a five-unit apartment building, two-and-a-half storeys tall with a communal garden and a private parking court.

The application says the plans would involve shortening the course’s 18th hole, with the loss to be offset by funding for “much-needed improvements” to other club facilities. National planning policy seeks to resist the loss of sports facilities unless they are surplus to requirement or would be replaced by equal or better facilities.

The club was established in 1912 and says the site is in an “exceptionally sustainable location” close to Cooden Beach railway station.

title: Westfield says farewell to Christmas Lights co-founder Ken Munday BEM
text:
Westfield, outside Hastings, has paid its respects to Ken Munday, who was awarded the British Empire Medal for his services to the village.

He died aged 96 on 5 October and was one of the people who started the annual Westfield Christmas Lights, which has raised more than £130,000 for charity over its more than 50 years.

A procession left Churchfields on Monday and made its way through the village to Westfield Church, where his funeral service took place. A further service was held at Hastings Crematorium for those unable to attend, and the family invited people to The New Inn afterwards to share memories and raise a glass to Ken.

Ken and his wife Brenda, with their neighbours Wilf and Jean, put Christmas lights in their windows in December 1975, which led to the annual village event, the family said.

title: Toilets top of residents' list in £21.5m Pride in Place survey
text:
New toilets have topped the list of improvements residents want in Hastings, after MP Helena Dollimore asked how the £21.5 million of Government Pride in Place funding should be spent.

More than 100 residents responded to the MP's appeal, and many called for new town centre toilets. The main town centre toilet block was closed in April 2017 after Hastings Borough Council shut the facilities to make budget savings, and the site has been boarded up since.

The only toilets currently in the town centre are a small unit at the top of Priory Meadow, closer to Hastings railway station. Recent improvements from the funding have included more litter bins appearing and a new seafront sign directing people to the shops, restaurants and galleries beneath Earls Court.

One resident said: “Our lack of toilets and beach showers is a disgrace. Businesses cannot be expected to offer all the toilet facilities in the town.”

title: Free parking at Hastings council car parks in December
text:
Hastings Borough Council has agreed plans to provide free parking at its council-owned car parks on specific dates in the run-up to Christmas.

Parking will be free after 2pm on Saturdays 5, 12 and 19 December, and on Friday 25 December, Saturday 26 December and Friday 1 January. On the Christmas and New Year dates, parking will be free until charges restart the following morning.

The initiative is part of a wider package of measures to support the local economy. The council has also written to East Sussex County Council asking for free on-street parking, and Southeastern and Stagecoach have been asked to consider offering free travel initiatives.

The announcement came as Hastings MP Helena Dollimore was pressing for free Saturday parking dates in December to bring Hastings into line with surrounding towns such as Bexhill, Battle and Rye.

title: Bexhill councillor calls parking permit charges 'extortionate'
text:
A Bexhill town councillor has branded the price of residential parking permits in the town 'extortionate and over the top'.

Cllr John Lee raised the issue at a town council meeting on October 28 and tabled a motion asking the council to write to East Sussex County Council to raise 'serious concerns'. He said the recent restructuring of permit fees has seen some residential permits rise drastically, with residents forced to pay up to £115 for a first vehicle and £154 for a second, which he called 'an unfair tax on simply living in central Bexhill'.

He said the charges were £27 in 2019 and asked for a formal review of why they have gone up, saying he wanted to know where the money is going.

Cllr Tony Carroll said residents need to see what value they are getting for their money. Cllr Paul Wilson said the parking controls were brought in a few years ago after issues affecting staff working in town shops and businesses, and that the council would use some other measure if it did not use emissions.

title: Former St Leonards church becomes community hub with weekly market
text:
A former church in St Leonards has become a thriving community hub, hosting a popular weekly market and serving as a venue for concerts and events.

In 2019, Chris Ostwald bought the St Leonards-on-Sea Congregational Church at the corner of London Road and Pevensey Road, after other people interested in the building wanted to turn it into flats. He has since been restoring it largely on his own.

The church market, which started just over two years ago, has become a weekly attraction with food, drink and independent stallholders. The venue is planning classical concerts and gigs, with more lighting, stage and sound equipment on the way, and there are plans for a big café on the front steps overlooking the sea.

Ostwald's fiancée, Rong Jiang, oversees social media and event organisation, and the pair have recently taken on a market and venue manager. The project was highlighted in an episode of Homes Under the Hammer in October 2022. Ostwald said he plans to put in the deeds that the building can never be turned into flats, guaranteeing its future as a community asset.

title: Police make 18 weekend arrests in Hastings and Rother
text:
Sussex Police made 18 arrests in Hastings and Rother between 30 October and 1 November, a spokesperson said.

The arrests included seven for assault, two for theft of a motor vehicle, two for possession of class A drugs with intent to supply, and one each for drunk and disorderly behaviour, drink driving, shop theft, recall to prison and breach of a harm order.

Police said officers had remained on patrol over the weekend and responded to a range of incidents, alongside continued proactive work to identify and deal with those suspected of committing offences.

title: Rye station to close from 3pm for bonfire celebrations
text:
Southern has announced that Rye railway station will be closed from 3pm on the day of the town's bonfire celebrations, Saturday, 14 November, until the regular start of service the next day, Sunday.

Southern Rail Area Manager Paul Wyborn said the closure would follow previous years and would be for reasons of public safety.

Chief Inspector Sarah Taylor of Sussex Police said police officers would work closely with partners to maintain order, prevent crime and respond swiftly to any incidents during the event.

title: Police increase patrols in Eldridge Way area of St Leonards
text:
Police said they are increasing patrols in and around Eldridge Way, St Leonards, near The Ridge, following reports of anti-social behaviour from local residents.

A police spokesperson said officers understood the effect anti-social behaviour could have on residents and the wider community, and that they were increasing their presence in the area, listening to local concerns and working with partner agencies.

The spokesperson said residents affected by anti-social behaviour should report it, as reports help build a clearer picture and target patrols. Concerns can be reported online or by calling 101, and 999 should be called in an emergency.

title: On this day 1896: This week in 1896: first moving pictures shown on St Leonards Pier
text:
This week in 1896, the first moving pictures to be shown in Hastings and St Leonards were seen on St Leonards Pier, the local record shows.

The screening took place on 7 November 1896, making the pier the venue for the town's earliest public moving pictures.

St Leonards Pier had been built as a public amenity, its structure of iron columns and girders similar to Hastings Pier, and it went on to play a part in the social and cultural life of the town.

The pier's pavilion was turned into a fashionable lounge called the Kursaal in 1904.

It was closed and requisitioned by the military at the outbreak of the Second World War, and in 1940 a section of it was removed as a defence measure. It was damaged by a bomb attack that October and hit by severe gales in early 1943.

The final stages of removing the pier's piles were carried out in the summer of 1953, and there is now no surviving remnant of St Leonards Pier.

A trace of the 1896 showing survives today. A small, almost illegible sign on the promenade railings commemorates the film show, alongside an information board near where the pier once stood.

title: Coalition says October's budget cut the Warm Homes Plan by up to £5.7bn
text:
A fuel poverty coalition says the government's October budget failed to protect households on the coast from volatile gas prices, and cut the Warm Homes Plan by up to £5.7 billion.

Energise Sussex Coast, which works across the Rother area, and the End Fuel Poverty Coalition said the headline £100 Household Energy Payment for households in council tax bands A to D 'will barely dent' the predicted rise in bills, which are forecast to grow by around £300 a year over 2027.

The coalition said the budget included some welcome measures, such as extending the zero rate of VAT on domestic electricity to 1 July 2027, but that 'we got more piecemeal support and vague future promises'.

The cut to the Warm Homes Plan amounts to a £1 billion direct reduction to fund military spending, plus a further £4.7 billion of hidden cuts in a reallocation of the so-called 'financial transactions' pot. According to Carbon Brief, that could cut funding for the plan from £15bn to as little as £9bn. The £1bn direct cut was achieved mainly by slashing the Boiler Upgrade Scheme, which subsidises the replacement of gas boilers with heat pumps, described in the article as the 'central technology' for reducing the climate impact of heating.

title: Martin Cohen to launch new book at Hastings Palestine Solidarity event
text:
Bestselling philosophy writer Martin Cohen is returning to Hastings to launch his latest book on Wednesday 11 November.

Cohen, who has written more than 20 books that have sold over a million copies, returned to the East Sussex coast 18 months ago after years working in Australia and France. His new book, 'Israel-Palestine and The Case for One State', takes what the article calls an 'uncompromising look at the foundational philosophies of the Israeli state'.

The event, hosted by the Hastings & District Palestine Solidarity Campaign, will be held at Stade Hall in Hastings from 7pm. Readers will be able to hear from Cohen about the book, buy a copy and share an authentic Palestinian meal.

Cohen, who was born in Brighton, said: 'It is the journalist's responsibility not only to tell the truth but to make sense of events, and I felt this wasn't happening in the case of Gaza.'

title: Hastings joins in the 'Dusking' morris-dancing tradition
text:
A new autumn ritual called 'Dusking' has reached the Hastings seafront, bringing morris dancing to the town's darkening days.

Invented by Leeds-based folk artist and morris dancer Lucy Wright as an autumn complement to May Day, the ritual has no rules: people dance or do their own thing as the sun goes down on Hallowe'en night.

Members of the Rheda's Dream morris side and friends gathered at the beach at the foot of London Road for the occasion, where they danced, sang and shared hot chocolate and soul cakes around a fire.

More 'dusking' took place at Hastings Castle on 1 November, the article said. Hastings, it notes, is always enthusiastic to welcome new rituals.

title: Eight Hastings and Bexhill residents arrested outside US embassy
text:
Eight residents of Hastings and Bexhill were arrested outside the US embassy in London on Saturday 31 October, the Hastings Online Times reported. The group was peacefully holding signs reading 'I oppose genocide. I support Palestine Action'.

The Metropolitan Police put the total number of arrests made that day at 325, most or all of which took place under near-identical circumstances, the article said.

The arrests came as the UK Supreme Court is due to hear an appeal by Palestine Action co-founder Huda Ammori on the legality of the ban on the organisation, on 4 and 5 November.

title: Battle Bonfire returns to the Abbey Green on Saturday
text:
Battle holds what is said to be the oldest Guy Fawkes bonfire celebrations in England on Saturday 7 November, with the town's tradition tracing back to 1646. St Mary's Church then allocated two shillings and sixpence for gunpowder treason rejoicing, and the Battel Bonfire Boyes have kept the custom alive ever since.

The day begins with a maroon at six in the morning, and the Oldest Guy in the World is led onto the Abbey Green at ten in the morning by Saxon Warriors and a children's procession. A torch-lit procession, joined by bonfire societies from across the county, winds down the High Street before the bonfire is lit on the green outside Battle Abbey and a firework display is set off in front of the Abbey gates.

Battle's Guy has a pear-wood head carved from a local tree in 1795; the body is burned each year but the head is kept for the following one. Roads around the Abbey, including the High Street and Market Road, close to traffic from six in the evening until midnight, and there is no parking on the procession route. Trains are running to Battle from Hastings in the evening. The Bonfire Boyes say the event is not suitable for young children or those with a nervous disposition, and ask people not to bring their own fireworks.

title: Bexhill care home wins Pet Friendly Care Home Award
text:
Elizabeth Court Rest Home in Hastings Road, Bexhill, has won the Pet Friendly Care Home Award for 2026. The home, which provides residential care for older people, lets its residents bring their own pets with them when they move in.

Annie Parker, who manages the home, said pets are 'a big part of our lives, and it's heartbreaking when we have to give them up', so the home allows residents to keep them. At the moment there are three dogs, called Gizmo, Poppy and Pringle, and one cat, Tash.

Martin Ballard, who looks after the animals, said they bring 'so much joy to everyone', adding that the whole home benefits, not just the owners. 'As soon as you enter the front door, you're greeted with lots of wagging tails and happy dogs.'

title: Free off-grid solar workshops coming to Hastings and Battle
text:
Energise Sussex Coast, a local community benefit society, is holding free workshops on off-grid solar power in Hastings and Battle this month. The sessions are aimed at anyone who wants to build a small, fully off-grid solar system for a shed, workshop, van or truck, and no technical background is needed.

In Hastings, two workshops run from 6pm to 8pm on Thursday 26 November and Thursday 3 December at Central Hall on Station Road. In Battle, the workshops take place from 6pm to 8pm on Tuesday 17 November and Tuesday 24 November at the Battle Memorial Hall, run in partnership with Battle Solar Town.

Each location hosts a beginners' session on how off-grid solar works and how to plan one, followed by a session on sizing the system. Both are led by Energise Sussex Coast's 'green handyman', who lives off-grid himself and has built solar systems for more than 20 years.

title: Man convicted of 18 offences after shop thefts in Hastings
text:
Tom Marchant, 44, of no fixed address, has been convicted of 18 offences after a series of shop thefts in Hastings, Sussex Police have reported.

He was charged with 17 shop theft offences, 16 of which were committed during October at stores in Station Plaza and Castle Street. The offences involved goods worth more than £1,300, made up of meat, sweets and chocolate. He was also charged with possession of a Class B drug.

Marchant was arrested on 26 October and appeared before Brighton & Hove Magistrates' Court the following day, where he pleaded guilty to all 18 offences. He was remanded into custody.

Sergeant Sam Turner said business crime "can have a significant effect on those who live and work in our communities", and added that the result reflects the value of businesses reporting incidents and working with local officers.

title: Bird deaths spark campaign to remove netting in Hastings and Rother
text:
A new local campaign is calling for safer ways to manage birds around buildings after three incidents in which birds became trapped in netting.

Building Better for Birds was set up following incidents at Friston House and Waverley Court in St Leonards, Hastings Library, and B&Q at Ravenside, Bexhill. The group has secured a commitment from East Sussex County Council to remove the netting at Hastings Library, and has asked the council to review netting across its other buildings.

At the library, at least nine pigeons were found dead behind the netting. Seven bodies were recovered and two remained beyond reach, while a surviving pigeon, named Hattrick, was rescued with the help of Coussens Cranes and taken into the care of RSPCA Mallydams Wood.

David Walters, from the group, said its aim was to prevent further suffering and reduce the need for difficult rescues at height. Residents who have seen birds trapped in netting are asked to contact the group by email.

title: Residents brand St Leonards metal supports an 'eyesore'
text:
Residents have branded large metal supports in St Leonards an 'eyesore'.

They were put up following the demolition of the Battle Road arches in Silverhill, which the borough council said cost more than £1.16 million. The structure, nicknamed The Cage, has been the subject of complaints for several years.

On the Hastings Observer's Facebook page, Judith Haffenden called it an "absolute eyesore", while Catherine Scott suggested "just put some big planted pots there and clean it up". Others proposed a market or community allotments.

A council spokesperson said the arches were demolished to prevent them collapsing into the road, and that the support structure remains in place for safety reasons. Because the land is privately owned, responsibility for its maintenance, including clearing litter and vegetation, rests with the landowner.

title: Developers reveal bid to build 120 new Hastings homes
text:
Catesby Estates and Rurban Estates have revealed a bid to build about 120 new homes in Hastings.

The developers say they are preparing plans for a care home and housing on land east of Beaney's Lane. A spokesperson described the vision as "a high quality, sustainable and well connected development providing a range of house types and sizes, including much needed affordable housing".

The proposal would include approximately 120 homes, of which 30 per cent would be affordable housing, together with a care home, a landscaped public open green space, a children's play area, and pedestrian and cycle routes.

The developers are preparing an outline planning application and are inviting the public to comment on the proposals before finalising them and submitting applications to Hastings Borough Council and Rother District Council, via a consultation at catesby-hastings.co.uk. Catesby Estates and Rurban Estates are now inviting people to have a say on the proposals before finalising them and submitting planning applications to Hastings Borough Council and Rother District Council. The development would include approximately 120 new homes, of which 30 per cent would be affordable housing, a care home, a new landscaped public open green space and children's play area. Many readers have voiced concerns about traffic on The Ridge and pressure on local services, according to the Hastings Observer. Feedback can be shared via a consultation at www.catesby-hastings.co.uk.

title: On this day 1940: An air raid damages every house on The Lawn, St Leonards
text:
On 11 November 1940, an air attack reached The Lawn, a road of semi-detached houses in St Leonards.

According to the raid damage records, every one of the five pairs of semi-detached houses on The Lawn suffered some damage in that raid. Most of the houses were unoccupied or their residents away at the time. The damage listed for one house included 'many slates broken, large number of windows, frames etc. damaged'. The information given on the damage was usually even less.

Volunteers at Hastings Museum and Art Gallery are now transcribing the typed reports onto a spreadsheet. The reports consist of lists by street of the houses damaged in each raid.

title: Police appeal to find Orion, 15, last seen in St Leonards
places: St Leonards, Hastings, Rother villages, Bexhill
text:
Police are appealing to the public to help find a missing 15-year-old boy who was last seen in St Leonards on Saturday (31 October).

Orion, who was reported missing from Ninfield, was seen at 11.10am in the Crouch Lane area, a police spokesperson said.

He was seen in the afternoon leaving St Leonards Warrior Square railway station, and a released image shows him at Hastings seafront. He has links to Bexhill and Eastbourne, but police say he may have travelled to the Ashford or Romney Marsh areas of Kent.

He is described as slim, with short dark hair, and was last seen wearing a burgundy hooded top, blue jeans and dark grey trainers. Police said they were concerned for his welfare.

Anyone with information, or who has seen him, is urged to call 999 and quote Operation Shortgate.

title: On this day 1597: A storm swept away the old Hastings harbour
text:
A storm swept away the town's harbour on this day in 1597. Between 1595 and 1597, a large and expensive harbour, known as the 'pier', was built in front of Hastings Old Town. On 1 November 1597, a storm swept it away.

Attempts to bring a harbour back followed. James Burton, founder of the new town of St Leonards, tried but failed to raise funding for a harbour at the west end of Marina in St Leonards in 1831-34. Several ideas for a harbour at Hastings were considered in 1834-40, but came to nothing. In 1865, Britain's leading pier-builder Eugenius Birch produced new plans for just a pier, sited at White Rock. On 18 December 1869 the first iron pile of Hastings Pier was screwed into the seabed, a contract by Laidlaw and Son of Glasgow worth £23,250.

On 5 August 1872 the new Hastings Pier was officially opened by the Earl Granville, Lord Warden of the Cinque Ports, on a very wet and windy day. Known as the 'Peerless Pier', it was 910 feet long and 45 feet wide in the middle, and was unique as the first pier in Britain to be built with a large entertainments pavilion as part of its design.

title: Iden's The Bell pub moves closer to reopening after plans submitted
text:
A village pub that has been closed for years could reopen with three new guest rooms, after renovation plans were submitted to Rother District Council.
