The Bell Inn Iden Community Benefit Society has applied to refurbish the Grade II-listed pub in Iden, near Rye, The Argus reports. The former landlord's accommodation on the first floor would become three en suite guest rooms, while two existing letting rooms in the garden barn would be retained. The plans also include repairs to the building, a new fire escape door and external staircase, a single-storey timber-clad toilet extension, solar panels on the outbuilding roof and an air source heat pump to replace the gas boiler.

The pub closed in 2023 after tenants had lost money, and the previous owners said it was financially unviable. Residents formed the Save The Bell group after a village meeting in August 2023. A sale price of £425,000 was agreed in December 2025, and the society bought the pub in March 2026, having raised £312,000 through a community appeal that included £291,000 in share investment and £21,000 in donations.

The society aims to reopen the pub in summer 2027, with planning permission and listed building consent still being sought.

title: Status Quo's Francis Rossi to play De La Warr Pavilion, Bexhill
text:
Francis Rossi is to bring his solo Status Quo show to Bexhill this month. The guitarist will perform his Songbook: Quo – Past, Present, Future tour at the De La Warr Pavilion on Tuesday, November 10, the Sussex Express reports.

The set will include hand-picked songs from Status Quo's evergreen classics plus some deep cuts, and Rossi said he is also working up a new medley. "The pressure is on once more as I have put together a really packed new show for autumn of this year," he said.

He will be joined on tour by guitarist Andy Brook, who co-produced the 2026 album The Accidental with Rossi and appeared on the sold-out 2025 Songbook tour.

title: Local author Elizabeth Webb's new novel reviewed
text:
A new book by locally based author Elizabeth Webb has been reviewed by Michael Salmon in the Hastings Online Times. Dexter's Lot, published by BiblioMuso, follows its protagonist as he stumbles "from the exciting world of rock music to the mundane world of the supermarket," enduring many trials along the way.

Salmon describes it as an "exciting romp" that contrasts Dexter's extrovert, hedonistic nature with his vulnerability, and says he would like a sequel. The book is available in paperback at £9.95 on eBay and from local bookshops: Bookbuster on Queens Road in Hastings, Printed Matter on Queens Road, and The Bookkeeper on Kings Road in St Leonards.

It will also be available on buythebook from Friday, 30 October, the review says.

title: Secondary school applications close at midnight today
text:
Parents and carers in East Sussex have until midnight today to submit applications for secondary school places for September 2027.

Cllr Paul Soane, the county council's lead member for education, said last year 95 per cent of children were allocated a place at one of their preferred schools, but some families missed out because they applied after the deadline.

Applicants can choose up to three schools and use the council's online mapping tool to search for schools in their community area. Anyone who needs help can visit a local library, email admissions@eastsussex.gov.uk, or call 0300 33 09 472 between 10am and 3pm, Monday to Friday.

title: Beachy Head naval battle book published posthumously
text:
The final book from late Shoreham-based lawyer Quintin Barry, Beachy Head 1690: The Grand Alliance at Bay, has been published after his death in January 2025, aged 88.

According to the Hastings Observer, Barry was born in Worthing and educated at Eastbourne College. He qualified as a solicitor in 1958 and in 1970 led the merger of three Brighton firms to create Donne Mileham & Haddock, now DMH Stallard, serving as managing partner until 1988.

In retirement he published 20 books, mainly military history. His friend and former colleague Martin Allen, chairman of Shoreham's Ropetackle, said Barry had a lifelong interest in military history and that the final book continues his work on naval conflicts of the 18th and 19th centuries.

title: Christmas Makers' Fair at De La Warr Pavilion on 7 November
text:
Bexhill Artists' Workspace is holding its Christmas Makers' Fair at The Studio, De La Warr Pavilion, Bexhill, on Saturday 7 November.

The fair will run from 10am to 4pm. Items on sale include watercolours, ceramics, fused glass, textiles, children's books, bead jewellery and Christmas decorations, according to the Sussex Express.

Admission is free and there is disabled access. The 99 bus stops right outside the Pavilion.

title: On this day 2006: The last traders left Hastings Pier
text:
On 31 October 2006, the last traders on Hastings Pier left the boardwalks. The National Piers Society's news archive records that the businesses on the Promenade Extension, which had remained open, left on that day, and the final event was a Hallowe'en party in the Gritti Palace pub. By the end of it, the structure was padlocked and deserted.

A meeting to discuss the pier's plight was held at the White Rock theatre on 12 November. Mr Harmesh Pooni, speaking on behalf of owners Ravenclaw Investments, said they intended to carry out a full structural survey, which he hoped would be completed by Easter. Repairs to the damaged trusses were estimated at £1.5m, and the Conservative leader of Hastings Council said he would make no promises about compulsory purchase until the results of the survey were known.

The pier had suffered major storm damage in 1990. The closure did not end its story: the structure was 95% destroyed by a fire in 2010, and Hastings Pier Charity oversaw a rebuilding project, with the pier reopening on 27 April 2016, Wikipedia notes. The redeveloped pier won the 2017 Stirling Prize for architecture.

title: Hastings pizzeria Monellis named best in the world for 2026
text:
Monellis Sourdough Pizza, a family-run pizzeria in Hastings Old Town, has been named the best in the world for 2026, topping The World's 100 Best Pizzerias, a list compiled by international travel and venue-ranking platform Worth a Journey.

The restaurant, founded by Frankie Ruffolo and his wife Francesca Elia in December 2019, came first ahead of pizzerias in Italy, Japan and the United States. Mr Ruffolo and Ms Elia said: "We are genuinely surprised, deeply honoured and incredibly proud."

The heart of the pizzeria is a sourdough starter dating back to 1923, passed down from Mr Ruffolo's grandmother in Mendicino, Calabria. The dough is fermented for up to seven days, using traditional Italian methods.

A spokesperson for Worth a Journey said its rankings are calculated using a proprietary algorithm analysing millions of data points from hundreds of thousands of venues worldwide, with adjustments informed by in-person evaluations.

title: Rye farm says pumpkin crop ripened despite dry summer
text:
Pumpkin growers in Rye and the Sompting area near Lancing say they have produced a strong Halloween harvest, despite what the BBC described as the UK's hottest summer on record.

At Tibbs Farm near Rye, partner Phil Wheeler said the pumpkins were planted on south-facing land which had not previously been ploughed, and that avoiding weeds was an important factor in achieving a strong crop. Although the pumpkins did not grow as large as in some years, Wheeler said most ripened successfully: "They weren't big but they were ripened."

Farms in Sompting and Rye are welcoming visitors picking pumpkins in the run-up to Halloween, the BBC reported.

title: Rye's Mermaid Inn described as one of the UK's most haunted pubs
text:
The Mermaid Inn in Rye, a Grade II listed building, is said to be one of the UK's most haunted inns, according to The Argus.

The inn dates back to the 12th century, with the current structure rebuilt in 1420 and cellars dating back to 1156. Visitors and staff alike have reported unexplained phenomena throughout its rooms, and some refuse to enter certain areas alone.

Room 17 is said to turn icy cold without warning, with a rocking chair reported to move on its own, and chambermaids reportedly clean it in pairs. Room 5 is haunted by a "Lady in White", and guests have sent in photographs showing mysterious orbs.

The inn's guest book has included the names of Lord Alfred Douglas, Henry James and Dame Ellen Terry, among others, the paper said.

title: Ocean Symposium returns to Bexhill in November
text:
Bexhill is to host an Ocean Symposium and Marine Exhibition at St Peter's Community Centre on Saturday, November 14.

The annual event, from 10am to 4pm, is co-hosted by the United Nations Association Climate and Oceans, the Sussex Dolphin Project, Sussex Underwater and community supporters, with this year's theme "Reimagine: Beyond the World We Know, A New Relationship with our Ocean".

The day will feature talks from expert speakers, short underwater films and a range of stalls, with sea and river pollution and citizen science high on the agenda. The local marine ecology group Strandliners will be represented.

Tickets are available through Eventbrite.

title: Police appeal after car and horse rider incident in Bexhill
text:
Rother Police are appealing for information following a road traffic incident in the Broad Oak Lane area of Bexhill.

A spokesperson for Sussex Police said the incident was between a car and a horse rider, sometime between 1pm and 6.30pm on 6 September. The horse, described as white with black spots, was uninjured.

Police are asking anyone who saw the incident or who may have dashcam footage of it to come forward.

To help, email collision.appeal@sussex.police.uk quoting serial 433 of 19/10.

title: St Michael's Hospice opens Festive Market in St Leonards
text:
St Michael's Hospice is holding a two-day Festive Market at its Upper Maze Hill site in St Leonards on Saturday, November 14, and Sunday, November 15.

The market closes at 4pm on Saturday and 3pm on Sunday, with stalls selling local handmade crafts, jewellery, gifts and decorations, along with live music, festive refreshments and games for families with young children.

A Santa's Grotto cabin in the hospice garden is the highlight for children, where visitors can share their Christmas wishes, take a photo and receive an early treat; booking early is recommended to avoid disappointment.

There is also a Festive First Look evening on Friday, November 13, from 6 to 8pm, an adults-only browse before the crowds arrive. Spaces are limited. The event is sponsored by Percy Walker Solicitors and TE Connectivity.

title: Dee Day White retires after 34 years running yard in Courthouse Street
text:
Dee Day White is retiring after running a popular antique and bric-a-brac mews and yard in Courthouse Street, Hastings Old Town, for the past 34 years.

He opened his first shop, Anvil Antiques at 38 High Street, 61 years ago, he said, and after about 20 years bought a property in Courthouse Street where he opened a tea room and antique shop. With the help of friend Ian Porter, who bought the undertakers in the High Street with its large yard and outbuildings at the rear, he opened it as an arcade market that grew over the years.

He and his wife Beverley have decided to retire and spend more time together. The yard will continue to run on the same system, with Kelly taking over the till in place of Dee and Bev, he said.

title: New police policy will see illegal e-bikes and e-scooters seized from Sunday
text:
Sussex Police and Surrey Police have introduced a tougher policy under which riders caught using illegal electric vehicles in public could have their vehicles seized and destroyed.

Police are warning riders to think twice before taking illegally used electric vehicles onto public roads and spaces, with the new "no returns" procedure coming into effect on Sunday 1 November across Sussex and Surrey.

The policy will apply to e-scooters being used illegally on public roads or in public places, e-bikes that do not comply with Electrically Assisted Pedal Cycle regulations, and e-motorcycles being ridden unlawfully. It follows growing concerns from residents about the use of illegal and high-powered electric vehicles, which police say are increasingly linked to road traffic offences, antisocial behaviour and criminal activity.

title: Hastings Cabinet to discuss fee freeze and heritage funding on 9 November
text:
Hastings Borough Council's Cabinet will meet on Monday 9 November to discuss a range of reports, the council said.

The agenda covers financial updates, including fees and charges for 2027-28, a report on the external funding the council has received for heritage and leisure work, and an update on the Age Friendly strategy.

Cllr Glenn Haffenden, leader of the council, said the reports show the breadth of work being done by the council's officers, and that the council was pleased to be proposing to freeze many of its fees and charges to help residents with the increasing cost of living. He said the council had been successful in receiving external funding to invest in sport, heritage and leisure assets.

title: On this day 1940: The official end of the Battle of Britain, 31 October 1940
text:
On 31 October 1940, the Battle of Britain officially came to an end. The British recognise the battle's duration as being from 10 July until 31 October 1940, three months and three weeks of fighting that ended in a British victory.

The Germans had rapidly overwhelmed France and the Low Countries in the Battle of France, leaving Britain to face the threat of invasion by sea. On 16 July, Hitler ordered the preparation of Operation Sea Lion as a potential amphibious and airborne assault on Britain. On 1 August, the Luftwaffe was directed to achieve air superiority over the RAF, with the aim of incapacitating RAF Fighter Command; 12 days later, it shifted its attacks to RAF airfields and infrastructure.

It was the first major military campaign fought entirely by air forces. The Luftwaffe proved unable to sustain daylight raids, but its continued night-bombing operations on Britain became known as the Blitz, which lasted until 11 May 1941. Germany's failure to destroy Britain's air defences and force it out of the conflict was the first major German defeat in the Second World War.

title: New litter bins appear in Hastings under Pride in Place funding
text:
New litter bins are being installed around Hastings as part of the government's Pride in Place scheme, which saw the town awarded £20 million.

Projects are chosen by the Neighbourhood Funding Board, a panel of local residents chaired by Kevin Boorman, under three categories: up to £250,000 a year for public realm improvements such as bins, bus shelters and benches; up to £500,000 a year for community and leisure facilities; and up to £1 million a year for heritage restorations from year two.

Bins are already in place near The Stade in the Old Town, displaying the Pride in Place logo, with more on the way. Mr Boorman said people told the board they wanted cleaner streets. MP Helena Dollimore said more bins and cleaning equipment were coming, with vans later in the year emptying seafront bins more often and removing graffiti.

title: Rother District Council pre-election event for would-be candidates in May 2027
text:
Rother District Council is holding an online pre-election event for people considering standing as a councillor in May 2027.

Following the announcement that Local Government Reorganisation in East Sussex is paused and under review, the council said local elections scheduled for May 2027 are going ahead using the current district and borough boundaries, with all 38 seats on Rother District Council to be contested on Thursday 6 May 2027.

The session, via Microsoft Teams, takes place on Tuesday 24 November 2026 at 6pm. It is open to anyone considering standing, regardless of background or experience, and will hear from current councillors and senior officers about the role and the support available. Councillor Gareth Delany, chair of the Member Development Task Group, said becoming a district councillor was one of the best ways of influencing decisions about the community.

Places can be reserved by emailing democraticservices@rother.gov.uk by Friday 20 November 2026, and the session will be recorded and put on the council's website for those who cannot attend.

title: Eastbourne MP calls for shuttle bus between Eastbourne and Hastings hospitals
text:
Eastbourne MP Josh Babarinde has called for a dedicated shuttle bus between District General Hospital in Eastbourne and the Conquest Hospital in Hastings.

Mr Babarinde said the government "continues to drag its heels" over funding for a new hospital in Eastbourne. The Conservative government in 2020 pledged to build 40 new hospitals by 2035, including a rebuild of District General Hospital, while the Labour government revised the scheme in 2025, instead pledging to spend between £1.5 billion and £2 billion on refurbishing buildings at East Sussex Healthcare NHS Trust's hospitals.

"In the meantime, we need practical solutions to improve access to healthcare," Mr Babarinde said. He said getting between the two main hospital sites by public transport can take hours, forcing many residents to rely on expensive taxis to attend appointments, and called on the government to work with the NHS trust and local bus operators to make journeys between the hospitals "quicker, more reliable and more affordable for patients, visitors and NHS staff".

The call came before the autumn Budget was delivered on Wednesday. The call for a shuttle bus between Eastbourne District General Hospital and the Conquest Hospital in Hastings has sparked widespread debate on The Herald's Facebook page, according to the paper. Many people commented in favour of the suggestion, while others asked practical questions, including what happens when a bus is full or whether people would need to book. Some readers said the focus should instead be on restoring all of Eastbourne DGH's services.

title: Hastings business group welcomes Budget rates relief package
text:
Business representatives in Hastings have welcomed the government's package of rates relief for small businesses, announced by the chancellor, John Healey, in his Autumn Budget on Wednesday.

The Treasury said the package includes an extra 20 per cent relief for pubs, social clubs and all but the largest live music venues, in addition to support introduced earlier in 2026, bringing the total relief to 35 per cent. It said this support will be provided in 2027/28 and 2028/29. The Treasury also raised the Small Business Rates Relief thresholds for qualifying retail, hospitality and leisure properties to £18,000 for full relief and £21,000 for tapered relief.

John Bownas, manager of Love Hastings Ltd, which represents town centre businesses, said the group "definitely welcomes this news for many of our smaller shops and hospitality businesses", with the savings for some being "quite significant – thousands of pounds a year". Looking at the Business Improvement District area, he said there could be around 72 town centre shops seeing savings of around £250k collectively, rising to closer to £300k if the taper that currently applies extends to those with rateable values over £18,000.

title: Vacant Bexhill bank building to become two restaurants and eight flats
text:
Plans to convert the former Lloyds Bank building in Bexhill town centre into two restaurants and eight apartments have been unveiled.

Bozyel Construction Ltd has submitted the proposals to Rother District Council. The scheme involves turning the empty building at 11-13 Devonshire Road into two restaurant units at ground floor level, eight one- to two-bedroom apartments on the upper floors, and a rooftop extension.

A design and access statement from RX Architects, on behalf of the applicant, said the building occupies a prominent corner site close to Bexhill station and the seafront. The proposal aims to retain an active commercial frontage while bringing the vacant upper floors back into residential use, working within the constraints of the existing building and minimising intervention to its external appearance.

Lloyds Bank closed the Devonshire Road branch in September 2024 after it said visits had fallen over recent years.

title: New road signs installed in Bexhill for horse and rider safety
text:
New road signs have been installed in Bexhill as part of a campaign to make roads safer for horses and riders, a town councillor said.

Warning signs have been placed on Peartree Lane and St Mary's Lane, roads frequently used by horses and riders, Cllr Connor Winter said.

He said the signs serve as a reminder to motorists to reduce speed where appropriate, remain patient and give horses and riders sufficient space when passing.

"This was a commitment I made to residents during my election campaign, and I'm pleased to be delivering on it through continued work with the county and town councils," he said.

title: Hattrick the rescued pigeon is on the road to recovery
text:
A pigeon that was rescued after being snared in bird netting at the Hastings Library building is on the road to recovery.

The bird was near to death when it was spotted hanging from one leg from the netting which surrounds a tower at the library at Trinity Triangle. Local wildlife rescue group Wildlife Matters launched an appeal, and crane company Coussens responded by supplying a crane that allowed rescuers to free the bird.

The pigeon, which has been named Hattrick, was taken to the RSPCA centre at Mallydams Wood in Fairlight, thin and near to starvation. It was given water and eventually started to eat for itself and recover.

The report notes that it was too late for a number of other pigeons that became trapped and died.

title: Beach cleaners remove more than 15kg of rubbish from local beaches
text:
The Strandliners ecology group has collected more than 15 kilogrammes of plastic and rubbish from beaches at Hastings, Bexhill and Pett Level this year.

Volunteers took part in the sessions as part of the Great British Beach Clean for the Marine Conservation Society. The clean-ups also included a survey of what washes up on the beaches, and the litter data recorded by citizen scientists can drive ocean conservation campaigns and policy changes at local and national levels.

Unusual items found in the surveys included a sweet packet from Taiwan, a complete Bal-Ban egg from a 2007 container spill, and a message in a bottle from an Irish ferry.

The Marine Conservation Society said 4,126 volunteers removed a total of 2,231 kg of litter across the UK and Channel Islands during the ten-day campaign.

title: Rother to consult on 2027/28 budget with £2.72m in reserves
text:
Residents of Rother are set to be consulted on how the council will balance its 2027/28 budget, after Cabinet agreed on 26 October to consult staff, the public and, for the first time, individual organisations likely to be affected by savings decisions.

The council's general reserves stand at £2.72m, and it said it will need to increase discretionary fees and charges, increase council tax and make savings to deliver a balanced budget.

Cllr Doug Oliver, the council's leader, said extending the consultation to outside bodies was the right thing to do, helping the council make "an informed decision" that takes into account the views of communities across Rother. Rother District Council has launched its public consultation on the draft 2027/28 revenue budget, which runs until 5pm on Wednesday 16 December 2026. The authority said it faces a funding gap of £1.2 million while planning to spend £38m on services, and council leader Doug Oliver urged residents, businesses and community groups to have their say. Rother District Council has launched its public consultation on the draft 2027/28 revenue budget, which runs until 5pm on Wednesday 16 December 2026. The authority said it faces a funding gap of £1.2 million while planning to spend £38m on services, and council leader Doug Oliver urged residents, businesses and community groups to have their say.

title: Bexhill MP backs petition for 20mph limit on Pevensey's B2191
text:
The MP for Bexhill, Battle and the villages has backed a petition calling for a 20mph speed limit and weight restrictions on heavy goods vehicles through Pevensey and Westham.

Dr Kieran Mullan met local campaigners during a recent visit to Pevensey to discuss concerns about road safety and the impact of heavy traffic on the area's historic buildings, according to the Hastings Observer.

The petition, supported by Pevensey and Westham Parish Councils, The Mint House, English Heritage and local county and district councillors, asks East Sussex County Council to introduce the restrictions along the B2191, from Pevensey High Street to Westham High Street. Cllr Peter Lowton, chairman of Pevensey Parish Council, said the area was "suffering from more and more traffic", citing the Mint House's Tudor wall paintings and the 1,700-year-old walls of Pevensey Castle.

title: Hastings butcher releases calendar of 12 butchers for Mental Health UK
text:
Steve Fisher of P A Fisher & Son Family Butchers in Hastings is publishing a calendar featuring 12 independent butchers from across Great Britain to raise money for Mental Health UK.

Fisher said the idea started after he saw a Facebook post by Shaun of Fairweather's Butchers and Deli, and he wanted to shine a spotlight on independent butchers as traditional shops disappear from high streets.

Calendars are £10 each, with 1,200 being produced and 100 going to each participating butcher, and can be reserved directly from the shop. Fisher, who is now over four years sober, said he chose Mental Health UK because it was "something incredibly personal to me", and hoped his openness would encourage others to speak up about their struggles.

title: Hastings man to run Brighton Pier to Hastings Pier in memory of dad
text:
Conor O'Brien from Hastings has organised a 75km run from Brighton Pier to Hastings Pier in memory of his father.

The RUN4SMH event for St Michael's Hospice, which is based in St Leonards, takes place on 13 February 2027, with a group of 10 running the entire distance and others joining for stints along the way, O'Brien said.

His father, John, was 70 when diagnosed with oesophageal cancer in February 2025 and died in March this year after receiving care at the hospice. O'Brien said he first raised £1,700 for the hospice in a week by entering the Hastings Half Marathon. Further donations can be made through the JustGiving page.

title: On this day 1869: Frederick North, MP for Hastings, dies at 69
text:
On this day in 1869, Frederick North, the long-serving Liberal MP for Hastings, died, aged 69.

North had sat for Hastings across three spells: from 1831 to 1835, 1854 to 1865, and 1868 to 1869, according to Wikipedia. He was also a Deputy Lieutenant and Justice of the Peace for Norfolk.

His daughter Marianne North, according to Wikipedia, became a notable traveller and botanical illustrator. North's Seat, the highest point in Hastings, is named in his honour, and France can be seen from it on a clear day.

title: Portslade man jailed for eight years for rape and abusive behaviour
text:
Paul Savage, 50, of Carlton Terrace, Portslade, was sentenced to eight years' imprisonment at Lewes Crown Court, a Sussex Police spokesperson said.

He was found guilty on 10 July of rape, controlling coercive behaviour, harassment and breach of a non-molestation order, and was sentenced when he appeared at court on 23 October, the spokesperson said.

He had been charged on 2 January 2026 with intentional strangulation, possession of Class A and C drugs, stalking involving fear of violence, breach of a non-molestation order and controlling coercive behaviour, and was later charged with rape on 18 February, according to Sussex Police.

Detective Constable Lisa Turner said the complainant "has shown incredible strength and courage to come forward", and that Savage continued his behaviour while on police bail and after a court order was imposed, until he was remanded into custody.

title: Eight Hastings and Rother residents renew challenge to MP over Palestine Action ban
text:
Eight residents of Hastings, Bexhill and St Leonards who were arrested under the Terrorism Act have sent an open letter to Helena Dollimore MP, renewing their call for her to meet them on film to defend her vote to ban Palestine Action, according to the Hastings Online Times.

Palestine Action, a protest group that opposed UK arms sales to Israel, was banned in July 2025 when MPs, including Ms Dollimore, voted to proscribe it under the Terrorism Act.

The letter says the eight signatories were arrested for displaying signs reading "I oppose genocide. I support Palestine Action", and claims the ban "has already led to the arrest of over 3,000 people" and a de facto ban on new copies of Sally Rooney's books being sold in the UK.

The signatories say it is now more than ten months since they first wrote to the MP, and that they have not received a reply.

title: One in ten young adults in Hastings on unemployment benefits
text:
More than one in ten young adults in Hastings are claiming unemployment-related benefits, Office for National Statistics figures show, according to The Argus.

In September 2026, 10.2 per cent of 18 to 24-year-olds in the town were claiming benefits, more than double the 5 per cent average for the South East, against a 6 per cent Great Britain average.

That is a 1.9 percentage point rise on September 2025, when 8.6 per cent of Hastings young people were claiming, after the number had fallen by 2.9 per cent between September 2024 and September 2025.

Across all working-age people, 2,785 residents (5 per cent) were claiming unemployment-related benefits in September, compared with 3.1 per cent in the South East and 3.9 per cent in Great Britain. The most recent job density figures from 2024 show about 0.68 jobs per working-age resident in Hastings, against 0.85 in the South East and Great Britain.

The ONS warned that the shift from previous benefit systems to Universal Credit in March 2026 may have some impact on the claimant count.

title: Local energy advice service backs campaign to save Radio 4's You and Yours
text:
Energise Sussex Coast, the local energy advice service, is urging East Sussex residents to sign a national petition to save Radio 4's consumer programme You and Yours, according to the Hastings Online Times.

The BBC has decided to axe the programme next April as part of cuts aimed at generating £500m in savings for the corporation.

The petition, which already has more than 12,000 signatures, says the programme has been a voice for ordinary consumers for more than 50 years, exposing fraud and unfair treatment.

Kate Meakin, ESC's director, said You and Yours "provides a vital public service for all of us", and urged everyone to sign the petition opposing the decision.

The Hastings Online Times notes ESC, a community benefit cooperative founded in 2012, runs a free energy advice service that provided over £880k in financial benefits to households across East Sussex between March 2025 and April 2026.

title: Hastings to get £1.2 million Fairness Fund for community projects
text:
Hastings Borough Council has launched The Fairness Fund, a £1.2 million programme to support community-led projects that improve opportunities, health and wellbeing in the parts of the town where funding is needed most.

The council said the fund will be predominantly capital funding for projects that deliver lasting social value and help tackle inequality, with a focus on grassroots organisations and community groups. Applications are due to open later this year, with funding available from the spring of 2027.

A flagship project will be a Children's University Academy for Hastings, delivered with the London South East Academies Trust and East Sussex County Council. The out-of-school learning programme supports children aged five to 14 and is expected to bring extra opportunities to children from disadvantaged backgrounds.

Cllr Glenn Haffenden, leader of the council, said the fund was about 'investing in the people, places and communities that make Hastings special'.

title: Hastings and Rye firefighter receives 30-year service award
text:
Gary Bourn, from Rye, has been presented with a special award by East Sussex Fire and Rescue Service after 30 years of service, the Observer reported.

Mr Bourn serves with both the Hastings and Rye fire crews and follows a family tradition in the role. His father, his grandfather, an aunt, an uncle and a cousin all served with the fire service at Rye, he said.

Reflecting on three decades of call-outs, he named the 20-appliance warehouse fire at Rye Harbour, the days-long clearing of 500,000 litres of unknown chemical waste at Tradebe, also at the Harbour, and the fire at St Michael's Hospice as the incidents that most stuck in his memory.

He said the job differs sharply between town and country. At Rye, he said, crews have just five minutes to get to the station and get an engine on the road when the pager goes off, and in rural areas they can wait up to 20 minutes for extra help, whereas in Hastings additional fire engines and other emergency services can usually reach them much more quickly.

title: Residents call for action over former Hastings public toilets site
text:
Residents have called for the disused public toilets site in Harold Place, Hastings town centre, to be put to use, after stormy weather left a trail of debris at the site, the Observer reported.

A number of residents commented on the Observer's Facebook page, with suggestions including reinstating the public toilets, turning the site into a community garden, or making it green space with benches. One called for it to become a taxi rank or a larger bus stop.

The public conveniences closed in April 2017 after the council shut them to make budget savings. Council-led plans for a two-storey restaurant at the site were turned down by the authority's own planning committee in March 2022, with councillors citing residents' concerns about noise and traffic. The site has remained undeveloped since.

Hastings Borough Council has been approached for a comment.

title: Police launch Safer Town Centres campaign and new ASB powers
text:
Sussex Police is launching a month-long Safer Town Centres campaign across Sussex, backed by new powers to tackle anti-social behaviour, a police spokesperson said.

The new powers include what police called 'Respect Orders', which the spokesperson said give police and partners stronger tools to address persistent offending and protect communities.

Police said the campaign is aimed at helping people feel safer on the street, and will be used to explain how the new powers work.

title: Combe Valley Way to close overnight for bridge inspections in mid-November
text:
The A2690 Combe Valley Way will close to traffic between 8pm and 6am on Wednesday 18 November and Thursday 19 November, ending at 6am on Friday 20 November, East Sussex Highways has said.

The works involve inspecting a number of bridges to ensure they remain safe for motorists, along with repairs to damaged safety barriers, the authority said.

Work will take place between the Haven Brook Avenue roundabout and Queensway, with the road closed to through traffic. A signed diversion is in place via the A2690, A21, A2102 and A259, East Sussex Highways said.

Access to properties in the works area will be limited and managed during working hours, and motorists may experience delays or be escorted by site marshals.

title: Gorse cutting begins at Firehills in Hastings Country Park
text:
Hastings Borough Council is to cut back the gorse that grows in the Firehills area of Hastings Country Park.

Gorse is a native species whose dense, spiny thickets give cover to rare and declining birds including the Dartford warbler, stonechat, yellowhammer and linnet, as well as supporting a wide variety of insect life, according to the Hastings Observer. It is the bright yellow gorse flowers that give the Firehills their name.

The council's Grounds Maintenance Team is starting the third cut-and-collect operation in an ongoing project to restore the reserve's lowland heathland, the council said. Lowland heathland is a rare habitat recognised as a priority in the UK, and gorse, alongside bracken, can grow rapidly and outcompete other heathland plants.

The council said the area will gradually change from dense gorse scrub to a more varied heathland.

title: Police step up evening patrols in Rye after reports of anti-social behaviour
text:
Officers and police community support officers have continued with reassurance patrols in Rye and the surrounding areas, with particular attention given to Love Lane, Sussex Police has said.

The patrols follow reports of anti-social behaviour, police said.

Neighbourhood policing relies on information from the community, a Sussex Police spokesperson said, adding that when issues are reported, police can assess the concerns, increase patrols where appropriate and, where necessary, work with partners or deploy additional resources to address ongoing problems.

title: Hastings to receive £1m from the government's derelict buildings fund
text:
Hastings has been awarded £1 million from the government's Derelict Buildings Fund, according to the Hastings Observer.

Hastings and Rye MP Helena Dollimore said the money is intended to bring empty and derelict buildings back into use, put communities in control of valued local assets and help high streets. She named several well-known empty buildings in Hastings, including St Mary's in the Castle, the Azur, Queensbury House and the old Argos building.

The award is in addition to a £21.5 million Pride in Place fund the MP secured to improve Hastings over the next 10 years. She also said she launched a campaign earlier this year calling on Hastings Borough Council to use High Street Rental Auction Powers, which Rother District Council and Thanet Council, among others, are already using.

Residents will have a say in how the money is spent.

title: On this day 1966: The Queen and Prince Philip visit the Hastings Embroidery on the pier
text:
On 28 October 1966, Queen Elizabeth and Prince Philip visited the Hastings Embroidery in the Triodome on Hastings Pier, as part of their royal visit to the Hastings area in commemoration of the 1066 battle, the Hastings Observer reports.

The Embroidery was paid for by Hastings Council and made by the Royal School of Needlework in 1965 to commemorate the 900th anniversary of the Battle of Hastings in 1966. It is 243 feet long and consists of 27 panels, each nine feet by three feet, depicting 81 great events. It took 22 embroiderers 10 months to make.

It was displayed in the Triodome in the summer of 1966. The Triodome was a large domed and circular exhibition hall, 105 feet in diameter, made of aluminium, which cost Hastings Council about £12,000. It stood between the two shelters close to the promenade, replacing the moveable bandstand that had been there, which was sent to Warrior Square Gardens. It was officially opened on 25 May 1966 by Princess Alice, president of the Royal School of Needlework.

After the Embroidery was taken down, the Triodome stayed on the pier: the council sold it to the Hastings Pier company in November 1968, and in 1986 it was re-erected at Brighton Pier as the Dome.

title: Leaders of three councils urge government to raise Local Housing Allowance
text:
Councillors in Hastings, Lewes and Eastbourne have asked the government to raise the housing benefit rates that help people pay private rents.

The leaders of the three councils have written to Florence Eshalomi, the minister for homelessness, democracy, communities and faith, calling for an increase in Local Housing Allowance (LHA) across their areas. LHA rates, set by the Department for Work and Pensions based on local rent levels, should be updated each year, but the Hastings rate has not been raised since 2024, and before that since 2020.

Research cited by the councils shows that in Hastings, no two-, three- or four-bedroom properties were available to let at LHA rates, with only two one-bedrooms available, and no shared rooms available at the shared accommodation rate.

Cllr Glenn Haffenden, leader of Hastings Borough Council, said that with so few homes that could be rented at LHA rates, "many residents cannot afford to live here". He added that between 2013 and 2023, house prices in Hastings rose faster than anywhere else in England.

Across Eastbourne, Lewes and Hastings, 525 households presented as homeless and were owed a statutory duty over the last three months, and 1,008 households, including 1,041 children, are living in temporary accommodation.

title: 173 residents urge Hastings MP to publicly oppose Rosebank oil field
text:
A letter signed by 173 residents of the Hastings and Rye constituency has called on local MP Helena Dollimore to "get off the fence and publicly oppose all new oil and gas projects in the North Sea".

The letter, reported by the Hastings Online Times, was sent after the government approved the Jackdaw gasfield in the North Sea on Wednesday (21 October). It notes that the MP has not joined the 68 MPs who have signed the #StopRosebank pledge, which calls for opposition to the Rosebank oil field and a properly funded just transition for oil and gas workers and communities.

The letter also quotes UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres: "Every new fossil fuel project approved today makes tomorrow's heatwaves more dangerous, and our world less secure".

Hastings climate campaigner Jane Ripley, who signed the letter, said: "The UK should be a world leader on cheap, clean energy. What sort of message does it send to the other countries we are asking to decarbonise if we renege on the spirit of manifesto pledges at the first opportunity?"

The Hastings Online Times reports that the government has conceded the Jackdaw decision will have little or no impact on people's energy bills and will create only 27 jobs.

title: Residents can quiz Southern Water at drop-in at The Stade Hall
text:
Southern Water is coming to the town to hear from residents directly, with a drop-in at The Stade Hall on Wednesday 4 November, from 1.30pm to 6pm.

Senior leaders and teams from across the business will be there, the company said. The event will cover what is being done to prevent blockages, how the company is fixing misconnected sewer pipes that cause pollution, and what financial support is available for people struggling to pay bills.

Southern Water will also explain the solutions being introduced to reduce storm overflow releases into local rivers and seas.

A spokesperson for Southern Water said the events are held in communities throughout the South East so customers can meet the team and "learn more about the challenges we face together", and that each one is a chance to ask questions and find out more about how the company is improving its performance.

title: New crossings and lighting completed around Hastings station
text:
The improvement works around Hastings railway station have been completed, East Sussex County Council has said.

The project included new and relocated crossings, accessible kerbs, resurfaced roads and pavements, upgraded street lighting and targeted drainage improvements, the council said.

New Puffin crossings and upgraded traffic signals have created safer, wider crossing points for residents and rail passengers, and high-friction surfacing has been installed on steeper sections and sharper bends to improve safety for drivers and cyclists.

Cllr Peter Griffiths, the council's lead member for transport and environment, marked the completion of the works, the council said.

title: Police appeal after catapults reported in Bexhill's Egerton Park
text:
Police are appealing for information after reports of animals being targeted with catapults in Egerton Park, Bexhill-on-Sea.

Sussex Police said incidents of catapult use in the park had been reported by staff at Rother District Council and that there are concerns wildlife may have been targeted. A force statement posted online asked anyone who witnesses a catapult being used to target wildlife, or who has information about incidents in the park, to report it at the time so officers can attend and take action.

Neighbourhood officers have increased daytime and evening patrols in and around the park, the force said. In the UK, catapults are not illegal to own or carry in public, but using them to harm people, animals or property, or for anti-social behaviour, can be criminal.

These reports are not isolated. Last month, 25 birds were found dead at Chichester railway station following a suspected catapult attack, and similar incidents raised concerns in Hailsham earlier this year, the BBC said.

title: Bexhill seafront fountain replacement reaches procurement stage
text:
A fountain is to return to the front lawns of the De La Warr Pavilion, with the replacement project now at the procurement stage.

In a joint statement, the Bexhill Neighbourhood Board, Bexhill-on-Sea Town Council and Rother District Council said the partnership has moved the scheme forward to identifying a contractor. The fountain was the top priority in community engagement carried out by the Neighbourhood Board and forms part of its four-year Regeneration Investment Plan, funded through the government's Pride in Place programme.

Rother District Council, as landowner and accountable body for the funding, will lead the procurement, while Bexhill-on-Sea Town Council has agreed in principle to take on future maintenance, subject to lease and construction quality arrangements. Repair options for the old fountain were explored, but replacement was identified as the most viable long-term solution.

Abi Newbury, chair of the Bexhill Neighbourhood Board, said: "There is still work to do before delivery can begin, but reaching the procurement stage is a genuinely positive step for Bexhill." Rother's Cabinet has formally agreed to use funding from the Pride in Place programme budget to replace the Bexhill seafront fountain and splashpad, the council said. Cllr Hazel Timpe described the fountain as "a much-loved community asset" whose loss had been "keenly felt". More has emerged on the plans to reinstate the fountain on the front lawns of the De La Warr Pavilion in Bexhill. Rother District Council will lead the procurement process as both landowner and accountable body for the funding, and Bexhill-on-Sea Town Council has agreed in principle to take on future maintenance responsibilities, subject to lease and construction quality arrangements, The Argus reported. The project forms part of the Bexhill Neighbourhood Board's four-year Regeneration Investment Plan and is funded through the Government's Pride in Place programme.

title: White Rock Gardens could get covered padel and tennis courts
text:
Hastings Borough Council says it is being considered to receive £1.3million from the Lawn Tennis Association to develop a covered tennis and padel centre at White Rock Gardens.

The council said the funding would be made up of £1million from the Department for Culture, Media and Sport via Sport England, with £300,000 delivered through the LTA's Tennis Foundation. Alongside the LTA money, the council would provide £500,000 for a scheme creating three covered tennis courts and three covered padel courts.

Cllr Glenn Haffenden, leader of the council and lead councillor for sport and leisure, said: "The success of the pop-up padel courts at White Rock Gardens over the summer has shown that there is a demand for padel in Hastings, and this funding would allow us to bring covered courts that can be used all year round to help keep Hastings' residents active." Hastings Borough Council has announced it is in line to receive £1.3million of investment funding to construct a new covered tennis and padel centre, with a projected overall cost of £1.8million and the council pledging £500,000 match funding.

The £1.3million would comprise £1million from the Department for Culture, Media and Sport via Sport England and £300,000 from the Lawn Tennis Association's Tennis Foundation, with the deal still being 'considered' by the LTA, the Hastings Independent Press reported.

A complex of three tennis courts and three padel courts would be built, at least partly on land currently used for bowls, following what the council described as high demand for the two temporary 'pop-up' padel courts installed this summer.

title: Hastings Round Table donates £10,000 to Conquest Hospital appeal
text:
Hastings Round Table has given £10,000 to the Friends of Conquest Hospital's 2026 Equipment Appeal, one of the largest grants the Round Table has made in recent years.

The donation covers almost a tenth of the £101,000 the Friends are raising for medical equipment at the hospital. The money comes from the proceeds of the Hastings Beer and Music Festival, held at The Oval in July and run by Round Table members with more than 80 volunteers. The festival has raised money for local organisations since 1982 and has now raised more than £1.5million for local charities.

The appeal pays for equipment that sits outside standard NHS budgets, including 12 special care cots for the Special Care Baby Unit, 30 Holter cardiac monitors that let patients have heart tests at home, and a maternity resuscitator for a unit where around 400 babies are born every year.

Jo Clark, general manager at the Friends, said: "Every pound we raise stays at the Conquest, and this grant will help us buy equipment that makes a real difference to patients and the staff caring for them." Jamie Neal of the Round Table said: "Almost everyone in Hastings has a connection to the Conquest, so it was an easy decision to back this appeal."

title: Holiday lets, flats and shops approved for arcade blaze site in George Street
text:
Hastings Borough Council has approved plans for 20 flats, six holiday lets and four commercial units on the site of the former amusement arcade in George Street, Old Town, which was destroyed in a fire in January 2023.

The development, by Oasis Developments Hastings Ltd at 39 to 41 George Street, was granted approval on 22 October, with construction required to start within two years.

The site has long been a sore point for local people. Residents have described it as an eyesore and raised safety concerns about an unstable wall and hoardings that have blown down in high winds. In March the council said it would take enforcement action over the state of the site, issuing a Section 215 notice.

The three-storey building was previously an amusement arcade and nightclub. Sussex Police said the fire, tackled through the night by firefighters with 10 pumps, was treated as a deliberate ignition. Demolition was completed in August 2023. Residents have divided over the approved scheme. One, writing on the Observer's Facebook page, said: "We don't need holiday lets and more shops; we need housing." Others suggested affordable bedsits or a hub for young people, while a handful backed the development.

title: Appeal for information after quad bikes stolen from Nurdle charity
text:
Beach cleaning charity Nurdle is appealing for information after three quad bikes and specialist equipment were stolen from secure shipping containers in the early hours of Sunday 25 October.

Rother District Council has shared the charity's appeal, saying the offenders cut their way into the containers with heavy-duty power cutting tools at about 3:00am. The stolen equipment included two brand-new Honda quad bikes donated to Nurdle by Honda, as well as the charity's own operational quad bike, along with specialist tools.

Police are actively investigating and have reviewed extensive local CCTV footage, which shows the offenders leaving in a westerly direction towards Rye, the council said.

The theft has severely impacted Nurdle's environmental work. The charity has been helping Southern Water respond to the ongoing bio-bead pollution affecting Camber and the surrounding coastline.

Anyone with information, or who has been offered any of the stolen equipment for sale, is urged to contact Sussex Police or the Rother District Council Coastal Office.

title: Hastings Winkle Club remembers 30-year member Mike Trigg
text:
The Hastings Winkle Club has paid tribute to Mike Trigg, a committee member for more than 30 years who died on 6 October.

The club, founded by Old Town fishermen to fund a Christmas party for their children, says that tradition still survives today, and that Mike was a regular sponsor of it and of many other Winkle Club fundraising events. He was awarded the club's Silver Winkle for distinguished service and made a vice president two years ago.

President Richard Stevens said: "Mike's passing was tragic and happened so suddenly that it has left our membership in complete shock. I have also heard from many members of our Old Town community who were equally stunned to hear the sad news. All our thoughts are with Mike's family and those closest to him."

The Winkle Club will be represented at any future thanksgiving for Mike's life and will dedicate a plaque to him.

His daughter Melinda, who says he was "a kind, supportive and caring person who touched the lives of so many", invites friends and family to a gathering to remember him at 2pm on 7 November at the Hastings and St Leonards Angling Association, Marine Parade.

title: Remembrance Day service and civic parade for Alexandra Park
text:
Hastings' annual Act of Remembrance will take place at the war memorial in Alexandra Park at 11am on Sunday 8 November.

The Civic Parade, with organisations and uniformed groups, will make its way from the Town Hall, along Queens Road, towards the park, the Hastings Observer reported. At the park there will be a service, wreath laying and a march past, then the parade will re-form and make its way back to the Town Hall.

The Veterans Hub, at 45 Robertson Street, will be open to all for a social gathering following the event. People are asked to dress for the weather, as the ground in Alexandra Park can get muddy and slippery in bad weather, and the lights in Bottle Alley will be red in honour of Remembrance Day.

title: Bexhill Beach Garden lit purple for World Polio Day
text:
Bexhill Beach Garden was illuminated in purple on Sunday 25 October in a local symbol of the global campaign to eradicate polio.

Bad weather prevented the event taking place on World Polio Day itself, so the project, led by former Bexhill Mayor Lynn Langlands, went ahead on Sunday with support from the Rotary Club of Bexhill and the Rotary Club of Senlac St Leonards. Deputy Mayor Cllr Paul Peters came along and helped, and donations were accepted, with the amount collected to be matched 2-1 by the Bill Gates Foundation.

Robin Taylor of Bexhill Rotary said purple has special significance in the Rotary polio campaign: in many countries a child's little finger is marked with purple dye after receiving the oral polio vaccine, making it a symbol of immunisation and hope.

Colin Goldsack of the Senlac St Leonards Rotary Club said that since 1985, when there were over 1,000 polio cases a day in 125 countries, the number of cases is now down by 99.9%.

title: On this day 1891: The opening of St Leonards Pier
text:
This week in local history: on 28 October 1891, St Leonards held the opening ceremony of its pier.

The pier was hailed as a masterpiece of design and construction, according to the Hastings History website. Its main feature was a 750-seat semi-Moorish pavilion at the landward end. It was 900 feet long, but only 25 feet wide along its central section.

In November 1896 both piers staged 'animated picture' shows, making them the first cinemas in the town, with St Leonards showing a week before its Hastings neighbour. When the pier reopened in 1909 as the "American Palace Pier", about 4,000 lamps were fixed all over it, making it a big attraction in the evenings, and a new pavilion was built as a roller skating rink at the seaward end that summer.

When the Second World War began in 1939, St Leonards Pier closed and never reopened to the public.

title: Storm power cuts threatened water supply to the Hastings area
text:
Two water supply works serving the Hastings area shut down over the weekend after the storms knocked out local power, though taps kept running.

Works at Beauport in Hastings and Powdermill at Brede were taken offline after power interruptions, and a number of vulnerable residents on Southern Water's priority list had bottled water delivered to their homes on Sunday as a precaution.

A Southern Water spokesperson said: "Our teams responded to challenging power issues over a 48 hour period and we worked around the clock to keep taps flowing. All customers remained in supply as normal."

title: Man found not guilty of sex offences on Camber Sands beach
text:
A man from Kent has been found not guilty of a number of sexual offences against a woman on Camber Sands.

Mohammed Maatoug, 34, from Maidstone, was arrested in August 2025 after a woman in her 50s reported being attacked while sunbathing in the dunes on 25 August 2025.

He was found not guilty of two counts of sexual assault and one count of assault by penetration. The trial concluded at Lewes Crown Court on Friday, the BBC reported.

title: New management takes over 15th century Red Lion pub in Hooe
text:
The Red Lion, a 15th century pub in Denbigh Road, Hooe, near Battle, has been taken over by new management.

The pub announced the handover in a social media statement, saying it is open every lunchtime and dinner, Tuesday through Saturday.

According to tourism guide Experience Sussex, the building was originally constructed in 1495 and converted into a pub in the 1600s. It was once a haunt for smugglers and customs officers, and its attic housed a secret tobacco mill that is reputed to have inspired the saying "money for old rope", The Argus reported.

Customers said the reopening got off to a good start, with one guest praising the roast dinner on the pub's first day and another booking a return lunch after visiting on Saturday.

title: Plans to reopen Marina Pavilion in St Leonards held up in dispute with council
text:
The reopening of the Marina Pavilion on the St Leonards seafront has been delayed amid a row over council repair demands.

Sea Change Sussex, the not-for-profit regeneration company, says it has received multiple bids from firms wanting to take over the landmark leisure venue. All the submissions depend on building works being carried out and require landlord consent from Hastings Borough Council, a Sea Change Sussex spokesman said. The company said the council has served notice demanding the property be refurbished within six months, in a manner that includes the completion of works not due until the lease ends in 2077.

Sea Change Sussex said it has also had issues with vandalism, electrical problems and flooding from overflowing drains connected to the adjoining public toilets. The site was put back on the market earlier this year after long-running power supply failures were repaired, following its closure in January 2024.

The company is now seeking urgent discussions with the council to find a way forward. Hastings Borough Council said it has not received any formal approach about the concerns, but added: "We are really keen to see Marina Pavilion open again, as we know visitors and residents are."

title: Hastings Castle to get £288,500 from Historic England for repairs
text:
Hastings Borough Council has been awarded £288,500 from Historic England's Heritage at Risk Capital Fund for repairs to Hastings Castle.

The grant, combined with £200,000 from the council, will pay for urgent conservation work, including stabilising vulnerable sections of the curtain walls, conserving the tower wall, chapel arch and Collegiate Church remains, repairing the Ladies' Parlour wall, and addressing vegetation, masonry defects and other vulnerable historic features.

Cllr Julia Hilton, the council's deputy leader and lead councillor for shaping place, regeneration and community wealth building, said the castle was a key part of the town's and the country's heritage, and that the work was needed to protect both the scheduled monument and the public visiting the site.

Louise Brennan, director of regions at Historic England, said the funding would support urgent conservation needs while helping projects move towards sustainable futures. Following the £288,500 Historic England award and a £200,000 contribution from the council, the first phase of conservation works at Hastings Castle has begun, with specialist contractors removing vegetation from sections of the castle walls and the motte. The works are due to be completed by 16 November.

title: Hastings Philharmonic Choir to sing Schubert and Saint-Saëns
text:
The Hastings Philharmonic Choir's next concert, Songs of Light, brings two choral masterpieces to All Saints Church in the Old Town on Saturday 7 November.

The programme is built around Schubert's Mass in G and Saint-Saëns' Oratorio de Noël, the Christmas Oratorio. The choir will be joined by soloists including Beth Yates and Helen May (sopranos), Kerry Gentleman (contralto), John Twitchen (tenor) and Geoff Williams (baritone), with the strings of the Hastings Philharmonic Orchestra conducted by Marcio da Silva.

Both composers were young when they wrote the works. Schubert, aged 18, composed the Mass in G in six days in March 1815, and Saint-Saëns, 23, finished his oratorio in under two weeks before its first performance in Paris in December 1858.

Tickets range from free to £22.50 and are on sale via the choir's website, The Bookkeeper on Kings Road, St Leonards, and Bookbuster on Queens Road, Hastings.

title: Gruffalo parade to close Hastings Storytelling Festival on the Stade
text:
The Hastings Storytelling Festival comes to a close on Sunday, October 25, with a free Children's Day on the Stade and a Gruffalo themed parade through the Old Town.

Produced by 18 Hours in partnership with the Hastings Storytelling Festival charity, this year's festival, themed Connections, has been running in venues across the town over recent days.

On Sunday, the Stade hosts puppetry, music, walkabout acts and creative workshops, including Pirate Gem's Swashbuckling Adventure show from CBeebies, Long Nose Puppets, Circo Rum Baba's Pesky Pirates and Mermaid Tales on giant seahorses.

Festival patron Axel Scheffler, the illustrator of The Gruffalo, has invited guest author and illustrator Tor Freeman to join the celebrations. A spokesperson for 18 Hours said everyone is welcome to dress up and join the parade, lining up from 2.45pm to parade with local drumming groups and hand painted costumes created by carnival artist Donna Fox.

title: Fears of hungry children over half-term after holiday food vouchers axed
text:
Families across East Sussex have not received automatic food vouchers for the October half term after the county council ended the school holiday scheme, raising fears that vulnerable children could go hungry.

The vouchers, which supported households whose children receive benefits-related free school meals, were stopped by East Sussex County Council after the May half term, following changes to government funding. The previous Household Support Fund was replaced by the Crisis and Resilience Fund, which is intended for households facing immediate hardship rather than blanket holiday vouchers.

Barry Ashley, who runs The Grumpy Cook cafe in Hastings, said he understood the new fund was managed by Citizens Advice 1066 and was aimed at sudden financial shocks, which school holidays do not fall into. His cafe will offer free meals to children during the half term, with no adult purchase required, as it did over the summer.

Penny Downes of Rye Foodbank said in July that she was very concerned about the end of the scheme, and the Food Foundation's latest figures show 39.2 per cent of children in the Hastings and Rye constituency are living in poverty. Liberal Democrat opposition leader Cllr Kathryn Field said she was concerned the most isolated families might not access the support and that children risked going hungry.

A council spokesman said support is available for any family in East Sussex that needs it, and that the way it is delivered has changed in line with government funding changes. The council said it would spend £7.3 million over the next year through the Crisis and Resilience Fund, on services including debt advice, community food schemes, holiday clubs with meals and help with household essentials.

title: Manhunt for escaped prisoner with links to Sussex
text:
Police have launched a manhunt for a convicted prisoner with links to Sussex who escaped from a medical facility in South London on Friday.

The Metropolitan Police said Anthony Lloyd, 38, absconded from the unit in Lewisham at about 4.10pm on Friday after forcing his way out. He was last seen heading towards Catford, wearing a grey-blue T-shirt, black tracksuit bottoms and white trainers.

Detective Superintendent Melanie Pressley, who is leading the search, said officers were conducting various significant inquiries to find Lloyd and return him to custody. She said she was concerned he posed a risk both to himself and the public.

Officers believe he could be anywhere in London, but said he also has links to Sussex, Surrey, Thames Valley, Hampshire, Nottinghamshire, Derbyshire and Merseyside.

Lloyd was convicted in 2025 of actual bodily harm following an incident in Nottinghamshire involving three emergency workers. He was serving a 12-month custodial sentence and was transferred to the medical facility in September.

title: On this day 1823: New town hall market opens in the High Street
text:
On 25 October 1823, the new town hall in the High Street opened its ground floor to the market traders, with 14 stalls taking up their positions.

The foundation stone of the building had been laid just over four months earlier, on 2 June 1823. The market floor offered meat on Wednesdays and Saturdays, and fruit, fish, eggs and the like on other days, with the market closed on Sundays.

As the town's needs changed, the ground floor took on other roles, becoming home to a police station and a fire station. The building is now the Old Town Hall Museum.

title: Bexhill empty shops plan opens for public consultation
text:
Rother District Council has asked residents and businesses to have their say on a plan to tackle long-term empty shops in Bexhill.

The council is consulting on a proposal to designate Bexhill town centre as an area where High Street Rental Auction powers could be used. The powers, introduced by government, are designed to help bring persistently vacant commercial properties back into use and support high street regeneration.

A recent audit of commercial premises in the town centre found 55 vacant units out of 439 properties surveyed, a vacancy rate of 12.5 per cent. The council said the figure is slightly below the national average, but the audit identified clusters of empty premises along London Road, Sackville Road, Sea Road and Devonshire Road. Bexhill is being considered as a pilot location for any future use of the scheme within the district.

Councillor Christine Bayliss, cabinet member for regeneration, said the council wanted to hear directly from residents, businesses, landlords and community partners before any further decisions were made. The council said Bexhill still benefits from a strong mix of independent businesses and hospitality venues, but the audit highlighted concerns around long-term vacant units and ageing buildings. The council leader says the draft Local Plan consultation remains open until Tuesday, November 24, and the Tapestry development in Battle, which will provide 200 energy-efficient homes, has been shortlisted for the Best Development Award at the Inside Housing Development Awards.

title: Buses replace trains between Tonbridge and Wadhurst from Saturday
text:
No trains will run between Tonbridge and Wadhurst from Saturday 24 October until Sunday 1 November, as Network Rail carries out major work on the Hastings line. Rail replacement buses will operate throughout, and the closure extends to Battle on the final day.

Engineers will use the closure to renew worn slab track in Grove Hill Tunnel, just south of Tunbridge Wells, and to remove three temporary speed restrictions: two between Crowhurst and Battle and one between Etchingham and Robertsbridge. The restrictions were put in place after the record hot and dry summer left soil beneath the track drying out and shrinking.

Buses will also replace trains between Wadhurst and Hastings from 10.30pm on Saturday 31 October until 7am on Sunday 1 November. Scott Brightwell, director of safety and performance at Southeastern, said the work is an investment in the Hastings line and asked passengers to plan ahead and allow extra time for their journeys. Tickets from Hastings and Ore will be accepted through to Ashford International and onto London St Pancras highspeed services.

title: Thin White Rope's Odom and Kunkel to play the Jenny Lind in November
text:
Bassist-vocalist Stoo Odom and Roger Kunkel, both members of the Californian desert rock band Thin White Rope, will play the Jenny Lind in Hastings on Friday 20 November, according to the Hastings Online Times.

The pair, reunited as Odom-Kunkel, are touring the UK to release their new EP 'Sniffing Spirits', which marries desert noir guitar with recitation, low-toned bass and improvisation. They will share the stage with Stray Bentos, the Hastings-based evolving collective fronted by Jude Montague and Danny Brittain, on the venue's Latin-themed Friday evenings.

Asked why he has picked Hastings for the tour, Stoo said: "Y'all are real sweet. And it's a tiny version of my beloved San Francisco, but with foxes, slow worms, and jellied eels." The gig starts at 8pm and is free.

title: Hastings mother wins national road safety award
text:
A Hastings mother has won a national award for her campaign to make the roads safer, following the death of her son in a road accident.

Maria Dennis's 11-year-old son Harry died in December 2022 after being struck by an unsecured scaffolding board that fell from a flatbed truck while he was a passenger in his father's car in Hooe, near Bexhill.

Since then Maria has campaigned for tougher safety standards for commercial vehicles and safe load security, travelling the length of the country for conferences, presentations and workshops. She has also worked with Hastings MP Helena Dollimore, who earlier this year presented a petition signed by more than 2,000 people to Parliament calling for better safety standards in the scaffolding industry.

She and PC Barry Freeman of Sussex Police's commercial vehicle unit were named 'Outstanding Contribution to Road Safety 2026' winners at the UKROEd/NPCC Roads Policing Conference at the Radisson Blu Hotel, Manchester Airport.

"This award is for my boy, Harry," Maria said. "I will never stop championing for higher load security standards and road safety."

title: Police secure closure order for Hastings property
text:
Officers from the Hastings Neighbourhood Policing Team have secured a Closure Order for a property in Cornwallis Terrace, Hastings.

Sussex Police say the order was granted under Section 80 of the Anti-Social Behaviour, Crime and Policing Act 2014 following ongoing reports of anti-social behaviour, drug-related activity, and offensive and criminal conduct at the property.

The order came into effect on 16 October and will remain in force for three months. During this period access to the property is restricted to the landlord, emergency services and utility providers, and any unauthorised entry is a criminal offence that can result in arrest.

Sergeant Turner of Hastings Police said: "This action reflects our ongoing commitment to tackling the issues that matter most to our communities."

title: Hastings Greens split over national 'Zionism is racism' vote
text:
The chair of Hastings Greens, Justin Lee Wynne, resigned his post and cancelled his party membership on Friday, citing an internal dispute over alleged bullying and his 'deeply uncomfortable' reaction to the national party's October 4 conference vote declaring the party 'anti-Zionist' and labelling Zionism as racism, the Hastings Independent Press reported.

National leader Zack Polanski has said he would not personally have voted for the motion, and several local Greens have made statements of regret. Cllr Glenn Haffenden, leader of Hastings Borough Council, endorsed a Facebook post by national deputy leader Rachel Milward, who said the motion would have 'a divisive and distracting impact'.

The Hastings & Rye Liberal Democrats wrote an open letter describing the motion as 'reckless, divisive and counter-productive', while local Labour councillors, led by MP Helena Dollimore, asked Green councillors to reject the policy in a public statement within seven days.

The Hastings and District Jewish Community, calling itself 'proud supporters of Israel', questioned whether it could expect to be discriminated against by Green councillors, while five members of Hastings Jews for Justice published a statement objecting to 'the weaponisation of anti-Semitism'.

title: Alabama 3 acoustic show at St Leonard's Church
text:
Alabama 3 are bringing their acoustic show to St Leonard's Church, St Leonards-on-Sea, on Saturday 14 November, the Hastings Independent Press reported.

Formed in Brixton in the mid-1990s, the band fused country, blues, gospel, dub and electronica. Their 1997 debut album Exile on Coldharbour Lane established them as British originals, and its opening track 'Woke Up This Morning' became known around the world as the theme to HBO's The Sopranos.

Presented as Alabama 3 Acoustic, the concert strips away the festival scale for an intimate performance in the church on Pevensey Road, with Lol Hammond of Drum Club joining for a DJ set.

Tickets are on sale now for the 14 November show.

title: Hastings and Rye MP criticises Bayeux Tapestry ticket phone system
places: Hastings, St Leonards, Rye, Bexhill, Battle
text:
The MP for Hastings and Rye has criticised the phone line the British Museum set up for local residents to book tickets for the Bayeux tapestry exhibition.

The museum offered people from '1066 Country', the towns with the historic link to the 1066 battle, an early chance to book the latest tranche of tickets from Monday this week, provided they could prove they lived in the area.

But Helena Dollimore, the MP for Hastings and Rye, said constituents were being kept on hold for hours. One person booked after two hours and 38 minutes in the queue, she said, and another was on hold for two and a half hours. She called the system 'glitchy and shambolic' and asked why constituents had to work on a phone line when online booking was clearly possible for others.

A British Museum spokesperson said demand for the exhibition had been 'exceptionally high' and that the offer to residents was on a first-come, first-served basis. All residents remain able to book tickets as part of the general sale on 21 October, and a third tranche of tickets is due to be released in the new year.

title: West Hill Lift gets £531,000 from National Lottery Heritage Fund
text:
The National Lottery Heritage Fund has offered £531,000 in development funding to Hastings Borough Council to secure the long-term future of the West Hill Lift, the Grade II listed lift that runs up the cliff from George Street to Hastings Castle.

The money will pay for the detailed design work and planning consents the council says it needs before making a further bid for funding to fully restore the lift, which requires major work to improve accessibility and reliability.

A council spokesperson indicated the full restoration is likely to cost around £3.8 million, 'but it very much depends on what the development stage shows'.

Cllr Julia Hilton, deputy leader of the council and lead councillor for regeneration, said the future of the lift is 'a vital part' of the Hastings Castle project funded by the Town Deal, and thanked the Heritage Fund and National Lottery players for the grant.

title: Warm Homes Plan cuts would be 'terrible blunder', local energy service warns
text:
A local energy advice service has warned that cuts to the government's Warm Homes Plan would be a 'terrible blunder' for households across East Sussex.

The Hastings Online Times reports the government is set to slash funding for the plan in next week's budget, following a Guardian report that ministers were 'preparing to slash the amount of money available', including hundreds of millions of pounds from the Boiler Upgrade Scheme, which helps households switch from gas boilers to cleaner heating such as heat pumps.

Energise Sussex Coast, which runs a free energy advice service across the county, says the cut would hurt households, the climate and national security. Its director, Kate Meakin, said that in the midst of the current gas crisis it was worse for the government to cut funding for a plan that would reduce Britain's exposure to fossil fuel markets.

The move has also been criticised by the innovation charity Nesta, which said it would 'take the wind out of an industry at a critical stage of development'.

title: Hastings artist to launch book of paintings made through cancer
text:
Hastings artist Helen Slater will launch her book Uninvited on the afternoon of Sunday 25 October, hosted by The Peripheral Space Project.

Ms Slater, who works in acrylic, began painting on 31 July, the day she was told she had breast cancer. Colour, texture and abstract form became a way to express what she described as a cascade of words no one expected to hear: tumour, scans, hormone blockers, operation.

She kept creating throughout her experience, producing 21 paintings and a short diary that began as private acts of processing and calm. They were first shared at The Peripheral Space in November 2025, an event where the idea for the book was born.

Uninvited gathers the work into an illustrated collection exploring fear, vulnerability, hope, resilience and gratitude. Erica Smith, who worked with Helen on the design of the book, calls it 'a remarkable combination of words and her paintings'.

title: Council's free business support pilot to visit Hastings Old Town and Rye high streets
text:
A new free business support pilot will reach independent shops and businesses in selected East Sussex high streets, including Hastings Old Town and Rye, the county council said.

According to an East Sussex County Council spokesperson, the pilot brings free, practical one-to-one support directly to independent businesses in Rye, Seaford, Newhaven, Mayfield, Eastbourne Old Town and Hastings Old Town. Businesses can receive tailored advice and a clear action plan focused on their own priorities, with support on topics including sales, customer loyalty, marketing, pricing, profitability and making better use of retail space.

The outreach team will visit businesses directly, the council said. The programme is funded by HM Government, East Sussex County Council and the East Sussex Growth Hub, and is managed by the county council and delivered by Smarter Society.

title: On this day 1944: Hastings' secret evacuation plans revealed
text:
On Saturday 21 October 1944, the Hastings and St Leonards Observer printed what the town had not been allowed to know during the war: the full story of the secret plans to evacuate the whole borough in the event of a German invasion.

Complete plans had been prepared for the compulsory evacuation of everyone still in Hastings after the voluntary schemes, with only about a thousand people, Home Guard, civil defence and essential services staff, required to stay behind. The scheme ran in stages: school-age children first, then the remaining civilians, and a joint plan for a grave and immediate emergency.

The Observer described how the Southern Railway worked out a secret timetable of special trains from all five stations between Ore and West Marina, each to carry 800 people, with the entire movement to be finished in three days. Extra luggage had to be packed and left at set points in town for forwarding to reception areas in Kent and Surrey, because evacuees could take only light hand luggage, and a circular went to every mother in September 1941 listing what her child would need to bring.

The plans were kept under revision until late in the war; the Regional Commissioner's direction was only cancelled at the end of September 1944. Hastings was spared the need for them, but the Observer noted the town's civilian preparations would have stood the test and 'a vital factor in the defence of Britain'.
